## About This User Guide

This guide describes the WaveView waveform viewer. The WaveView tool is a graphical waveform viewing and analysis program for analog/mixed-signal IC design simulations, which can help you to use simulation tools more effectively.

This preface includes the following sections:

- New in This Release
- Related Products, Publications, and Trademarks
- Conventions
- Customer Support
- Statement on Inclusivity and Diversity

## New in This Release

Information about new features, enhancements, and changes, known limitations, and resolved Synopsys Technical Action Requests (STARs) is available in the WaveView Release Notes on the SolvNetPlus site.

## Conventions

The following conventions are used in Synopsys documentation.

| Convention     | Description                                                                                                                                                           |
|----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Courier        | Indicates syntax, such as write_file .                                                                                                                                |
| Courier italic | Indicates a user-defined value in syntax, such as write_file design_list                                                                                              |
| Courier bold   | Indicates user input-text you type verbatim-in examples, such as prompt> write_file top                                                                               |
| Purple         | • Within an example, indicates information of special interest. • Within a command-syntax section, indicates a default, such as include_enclosing = true &#124; false |
| [ ]            | Denotes optional arguments in syntax, such as write_file [-format fmt ]                                                                                               |
| ...            | Indicates that arguments can be repeated as many times as needed, such as pin1 pin2 ... pinN .                                                                        |
| &#124;         | Indicates a choice among alternatives, such as low &#124; medium &#124; high                                                                                          |
| \              | Indicates a continuation of a command line.                                                                                                                           |
| /              | Indicates levels of directory structure.                                                                                                                              |
| Bold           | Indicates a graphical user interface (GUI) element that has an action associated with it.                                                                             |

## Statement on Inclusivity and Diversity

Synopsys is committed to creating an inclusive environment where every employee, customer, and partner feels welcomed. We are reviewing and removing exclusionary language from our products and supporting customer-facing collateral. Our effort also includes internal initiatives to remove biased language from our engineering and working environment, including terms that are embedded in our software and IPs. At the same time, we are working to ensure that our web content and software applications are usable to people of varying abilities. You may still find examples of non-inclusive language in our software or documentation as our IPs implement industry-standard specifications that are currently under review to remove exclusionary language.

## Getting Started

This chapter details getting started with the WaveView tool.

The WaveView tool is a graphical waveform viewing and analysis program for analog/ mixed-signal IC design simulations, which can help you to use simulation tools more effectively with:

- High-performance waveforms database I/O to access large amount of simulation data efficiently.
- Extensive mixed-signal display functions and analysis capabilities to extract design parameters from simulation result.

This chapter contains information on the following topics:

- Setting Up
- Basic WaveView Usage
- Basic GUI Usage
- Running ACE Scripts

## Setting Up

This section contains information on the following topics:

- Starting the Tool
- Setting Environment Variables
- Setting up the MATLAB Interface to WaveView
- Customizing File Browser Filters
- Configuring "Send To" in the Windows Environment
- Configuring the WaveView Tool Manually

<!-- image -->

## Starting the Tool

Before starting the WaveView tool, consider any environment options you might want to set. See Setting Environment Variables for more information.

On Linux platforms, enter wv at the command line to start the WaveView tool.

## Note:

If you have a WaveView ADV license and want to enable ADV features, enter wv -adv at the command line to start the tool.

See Supported Command-Line Options for a list of available command-line options you can use when starting the WaveView tool.

## Invoking the WaveView Tool With a Design or Netlist

## Note:

This feature requires a WaveView ADV license.

You can invoke the WaveView tool from the command line.

To invoke the WaveView with a netlist or design, enter the following line at the command line from the location where you have your design saved:

<!-- formula-not-decoded -->

Your design opens in a design tab in the WaveView window.

All displayed sections are synchronized in a DesignView. For example, when you select a scope in the Design Hierarchy , the Signal List displays all signals in the current cell, the SourceView display jumps to the first line of the cell definition, and the ConnectionView displays the relative cells as well.

## Note:

Unless you are opening a previously saved session, the LintView pane might not be visible. See Displaying the LintView on Startup for more information on making the LintView window visible whenever you invoke the WaveView tool.

## WaveView ADV License Features

The following features are only available if you have a WaveView ADV license.

- Importing and working with designs
- Waveform compare
- DDR measurements

<!-- image -->

- ACE scripting
- Channel Simulation Analyses (CSA)

## Setting Environment Variables

When starting the WaveView tool, you might want to set one or more of the following environment variables.

- SW\_SX\_QUEUE\_LIC (not supported on Windows platforms) enviro m t  a bl sSW\_QUE LIC Set to 1 to enable the license queuing feature for all WaveView licenses (including CDS\_link licenses). Flexlm license queuing is not yet supported.
- SW\_SX\_FAST\_COU

Set to 1 to enable the fast COU file reader (the default is 0). Fast COU reader reads multi-run COU files much faster.

- ·
- SW\_SX\_FAST\_JWDB enviro m t  a bl sSW\_ X FA T J DB Set to 1 to enable the fast WDB file reader (the default is 1). Fast WDB reader does not require the Java server.
- SW\_SX\_HELP (Linux only)

Points to the directory that contains the WaveView online help.

- SW\_SX\_INIT enviro m t  a bl sSW\_ X IN T Defines the initialization file ( .spxinit ) for the top-level customization. Ensure you set

this variable to the .spxinit file name you use.

- SW\_SX\_INIT\_DIR enviro m t  a bl sSW\_ X IN T D R

Defines the WaveView initial startup directory.

- SW\_SX\_LOG\_DIR (Linux only) enviro m t  a bl sSW\_ X LOG DIR Defines the output directory for the sxcmd.log log file. The default location is the current working directory.
- ·
- SW\_SX\_MASKFILE

Points to user-defined mask files for eye diagrams.

- SW\_SX\_NO\_ADV\_LIC

When set to 1, WaveView does not check out an ADV license in any condition.

When set to 2, WaveView does not check out an ADV license in WaveView-only mode (when invoked with command wv ); WaveView does check out an ADV license if WaveView ADV mode (when invoked with commands wv -adv , sx , or cx ).

When not set, WaveView does not block checking out a WaveView ADV license.

- SW\_SX\_NO\_APX\_LIC

Set to 1 to indicate that no sx\_apx license is present (the default is 0).

- SW\_SX\_ORG\_ADC enviro m t  a bl sSW\_ X ORG ADC

Set to 1 to use the old version of the ADC Toolbox.

- SW\_LIC\_TIMEOUT

Sets the amount of time that the WaveView tool holds on to a license when idle. Once the set time is expired, a dialog box asks you to either reclaim the license or exit and save the session. The minimum value is 30 (minutes). Supported for all license checkouts, including sx\_cdslink .

- SX\_WAIT\_LICENSE\_TIMEOUT

Sets the amount of time (in minutes) to wait for a license. When set, the WaveView tool exits when the license queuing timeout occurs.

- SW\_SX\_TK\_LIB

Points to the Tk runtime library for running ACE

- SW\_SX\_TMP\_DIR (Linux only)

Points to the temporary directory for reading a compressed (gzipped) waveform file. Default directory for temporary uncompressed files is the current working directory.

- SW\_SX\_USE\_AMAP (Linux only)

Set to 1 to use the map files in the Artist amap/ directory to map signal names.

- SW\_SX\_USE\_TK

Set to 1 to enable using Tk scripts in the WaveView tool.

- SW\_WLF\_READER enviro m t  a bl sSW\_ LF READ

Points to the wlf2sx executable for reading the ModelSim WLF format.

- SX\_HOME (Linux only)

Defines the WaveView home directory. The WaveView tool searches for the .spxrc file in $SX\_HOME if SX\_HOME is defined.

- SW\_SX\_64

Set to 1 to point to the 64-bit binaries.

- CX\_DRTAB\_FILE

Specifies a DRTAB mask spec files, which includes the following units:

- minimum target slew (in V/ns units)
- minimum target VIHL\_AC (in V units)
- minimum target TdiVW\_Total (in s units)
- minimum Tdipw (in UI units)

The following sample is a DRTAB mask spec file:

```
#ddr4_spec DDR4_1600 #ddr_ui  660p #vref_set_tol 0.15 #min_aperture 320p #min_dataslew 1 #min_tdipw_ui 0.58 #min_vihl_ac 186m
```

- SW\_SX\_NTHREAD

Specifies the maximum thread numbers to use for plotting and calculations.

## Setting up the MATLAB Interface to WaveView

The MATLAB interface to the WaveView tool includes features like reading in all WaveView supported file formats, including sweep signals (from group files as well), and creating parameter filters to read in only specified traces.

## Note:

For more information on MATLAB, see the MATLAB documentation from MathWorks®.

This section contains information on the following topics:

- MATLAB Interface Components
- Licensing Requirements
- APIs Supported in MATLAB Interface
- Limitations

<!-- image -->

## MATLAB Interface Components

A shared library is included in the WaveView tool installation, which includes reader code for waveform file formats that the WaveView tool supports. The shared library works in compiled MATLAB, and can also be used in other C/C++ applications since it is a standard C library. The 64-bit RHEL5 and RHEL6 platforms are supported.

A set of APIs is also included, which is used to open files, read signal names, read data, handle sweep signals, and close files.

The header file for the interface ( matapi.h ) is located in the following directory:

&lt;installation\_dir&gt;/etc/include/

The shared library for the interface ( libmatapi.so ) is located in the following directory:

&lt;installation\_dir&gt;/platforms/linux64/lib /

Before loading the MATAPI library on Linux platforms, first include the reader libraries in LD\_LIBRARY\_PATH . The reader libraries are included in the WaveView tool installation package.

## Licensing Requirements

WaveView license ( sx\_wva ) is checked out when you use the APIs in the library.

If an sx\_wva license is already checked out, the API is executed; otherwise, the sx\_wva license is checked out and the API is executed.

## APIs Supported in MATLAB Interface

Here are the APIs are supported.

| API Name                              | Function                                                                                                                        |
|---------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| HWRF wv_open_file(char *file_path)    | Opens a waveform file (including .grp files). Returns a void* type result, which is used as file_handle in the subsequent APIs. |
| void wv_close_file(void* file_handle) | Closes an opened waveform file.                                                                                                 |
| int wv_num_signals(void* file_handle) | Gets the number of signals in a waveform file.                                                                                  |

This API also performs the following functions: • Returns an array of signal names. • Saves the number of matching names in the INT4*count. • Returns only matched signals when a pattern is specified. Question marks (?) and asterisks (*) are supported in patterns. Note: This API might use a large amount of                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

This API also performs the following functions: • Returns the signal object handle, which is used as signal_handle in subsequent APIs. • Defines signal_type in the SIGTYPE enumeration. This can be useful for multiple signals with the same name, but differing types. • Stores the return bit index in pidx if psig is a bit of a bus signal. For example, A[2]. pidx is set to -1 if psig is an analog signal or if psig is a bus signal.                                                                                                |
| int wv_load_signal(void* file_handle, HSIG signal_handle, struct wv_sig_data **data) | Loads data for the given signal. Analog real, analog complex, digital, and bus signals can all be loaded. Single trace and multiple traces on analog signals are also supported. This API also performs the following functions: • Saves the signal data in struct wv_sig_data **data , which is an array of the wv_sig_data structure. • Saves the signal data in each element of data, which saves one trace of the data. • Includes the parameter name values if they exist, as well as the X and Y pairs for each trace. • Returns magnitude and phase Y values for complex data. • Returns the number of traces for sweep signals. |

If a parameter has string values, the string array is returned as the return value of the function. If a parameter has double values, the values are set in the double *dvals array. The number of values is set in int nvals . |

This API also performs the following functions: • Supports both string and double type parameter values. • Returns parameter conditions as array of the wv_param_cond structure. ## Using the WV\_SIG\_DATA Structure

The WV\_SIG\_DATA structure saves the signal data read from waveform files by the wv\_load\_signal function. For example:

```
typedef struct wv_sig_data { char *paramcond; // param and values for the trace, in format of "A=1:B=slow:C=-20" int tidx; // trace index in full load (without filter)int npts; // number of points double *xval; double *yreal; double *yimag; char *pVec; // digital/bus values, each value is separated by " " } WV_SIG_DATA;
```

You need to declare a pointer and then call the wv\_load\_signal function to load data. For example:

```
% open waveform file strcpy(filepath,"test.wdf"); pfile = wv_open_file(filepath); % Get signal object in file_handle psig = wv_get_signal(wfile,"v(out)",WV_SIGTYPE_ALL,&pidx); % load signal data sigdata = libpointer('wv_sig_data'); calllib('libmatapi', 'wv_load_signal',pfile,psig,sigdata); % number of points npts = sigdata.value.npts % get x and y value array xval = sigdata.value.xval; setdatatype(xval,'doublePtr',npts); xdata = xval.value yreal = sigdata.value.yreal; setdatatype(yreal,'doublePtr',npts); ydata = yreal.value % plot(x,y) plot(xval.value,yreal.value); % clear the pointer if you do not need the data anymore clear sigdata;
```

## Limitations

These limitations apply to the MATLAB interface.

- Structure Limitations

Nested structures or structures containing a pointer to a structures are not supported. However, MATLAB has access to an array of structures created in an external library.

<!-- image -->

## · Pointer Limitations

Support is limited for multi-level pointers and structures that contain pointers. Using inputs and outputs and structure members declared with more then two levels of indirection is also not supported. For example, double ***outp translated to doublePtrPtrPtr is not supported.

## Customizing File Browser Filters

The file filter option menu in the file loading dialog box can be customized to add your own filter patterns.

## To customize the menu:

1. Click Preferences in the Configuration tab.

The Preference Settings window opens.

2. Select the General category.
3. Specify a waveform filter from the Waveform File Filter preference menu.

You can choose to filter All Files or Waveform Files .

4. (Optional) Click New to create a new filter pattern, then enter your own filter pattern using the following format:

```
pattern_label:filter_pattern
```

The pattern\_label is a character string, and filter\_pattern is the actual string pattern used for name filtering. Both parts are displayed in the filter option menu. The pattern\_label can contain spaces.

- Multiple filter patterns are delimited by vertical bar (|):
- Multiple filter option menu pattern entries are delimited by a semicolon (;):
- Multiple filter option menu pattern entries are delimited by a semicolon (;):
- Globbing expressions are supported through wildcards:

```
Spice3 output:*.raw|*.out
```

```
Spice3 output:*.raw ; Spice listing:*.out
```

```
Spice3 output:*.raw ; Spice listing:*.out
```

```
Hspice:*.tr[0-9]|*.ac[0-9|*.dc[0-9]
```

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

If the pattern\_label field is omitted in an entry, the filter\_pattern is used as the display string in the filter option menu.

5. Click OK or Apply-save to save your changes.

To delete a custom filter, select the filter from the Waveform File Filter menu and click Delete .

## Configuring "Send To" in the Windows Environment

In the Windows OS environment, the WaveView tool can be added to the Send To application list to support direct import of waveform files or the WaveView session files using the Send To context menu.

To add the WaveView tool to the Send To application list:

- Choose  from the main desktop screen and enter sendtoStart &gt; Run to open the SendTo folder.

To support reading waveform files using the Send To menu:

- Add a shortcut in the SendTo folder to the WaveView executable. The executable can be found at C:/Program Files/Sandwork Design/WaveView version/wv.exe .

To support reading session files using the Send To menu:

1. Add a short cut in the SendTo folder to the WaveView executable. Make sure that the -x option is appended to the end in the Target field in the shortcut

property.

2. Rename the shortcut to reflect the purpose of the Send To shortcut ("WV Session", for example).

## Configuring the WaveView Tool Manually

You can configure the WaveView tool by modifying the .spxrc configuration file for Linux platforms or modifying the Windows Registry for MS-Windows platforms.

On the Linux platform, the configuration settings are used to initialize the WaveView tool.

- The configuration file must be named .spxrc . The WaveView tool reads the configuration file from four different locations in the following order:

```
a. -spxrc switch on command line b. current_working_directory/.spxrc
```

```
c. $(HOME)/.spxrc (if HOME is defined) d. $(SX_HOME)/.spxrc (if SX_HOME is defined)
```

SX\_HOME is a user-defined environment variable; HOME is a shell variable which defaults to a user's home directory.

Configuration settings from current\_working\_directory/.spxrc have the highest priority. Settings read first are overridden by those read later in the sequence.

- On a Windows platforms, preference settings are automatically updated into Windows Registry when you click Save in the Preference Settings dialog box (See Setting Preferences).

If manual editing is necessary, run regedit from a MS-DOS prompt and modify settings in the following location:

HKEY\_CURRENT\_USER\Software\Sandwork Design\WaveView

## Loading and Saving Sessions

The WaveView tool provides save and restore functions for users to save or retrieve a job session to or from a session file. Session files have the .sx default file extension.

- Save Session
- Load Session

## Save Session

Use this procedure to save your current session.

1. Before saving your session, you might consider changing the save directory from the default.
2. Click Save Session on the File tab.

The Save Session dialog box opens.

3. Select or enter the file in which to save your current job session.
4. (Optional) Click the Use Relative Path in Session File check box to use a relative path for your session file.
5. (Optional) Click the Save Current Waveview Only check box to save only the current waveview tab in your saved session file.
6. (Optional) Click the Save a Copy of Loaded Signals check box to save loaded signals to a new file named &lt;session\_file\_name&gt;.wdf .

For example, if a session is saved to a file called foo.sx , the data file name is foo.sx.wdf . When loading the session file, only foo.sx.wdf is loaded.

7. Click OK to save your job session.

## Load Session

Use this procedure to load from a session file.

1. Click Load Session on the File tab.

The Load Session dialog box appears.

2. Browse to and select the session file you want to open.

The browser opens to the last location from which a session file was loaded.

3. (Optional) To apply the saved signal selection/layout to other loaded waveform data files in the application, ensure the Apply to existing waveform files option is enabled (the default). Select the preferred waveform data file for each restore target using the Waveform Source dialog box.

If the Apply to existing waveform files option is not enabled, the session loader restores signal selection/layout using the waveform data files specified in the session file.

4. (Optional) Click the Suppress popup warning messages option check box to disable session loading warning messages (missing signals, for example).
5. Click OK to load the selected session file.

The session file is loaded into the WaveView tool.

## Note:

When loading a session file and applying it to multiple target files, an index number is appended to waveview tab names to avoid duplicate names. For example, for name waveview1 in session file, the displayed tab names become waveview 1\_1 , waveview1\_2 , and so on. The index starts from 1.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

You can also load a session file from the command line with the -x option. For example:

```
wv -x setup_file
```

Add the -y option to apply the session setup to different waveform data files. For example:

```
wv -y setup_file file1 file2 … filen
```

Log files are saved for every session.

You can also view log files from previous sessions, which are saved in your working directory as sequentially numbered files (for example, cx.log.1 , cx.log.2 , cx.log.3 ).

By default, the WaveView tool outputs log files in the working directory. However, there is an option to change the default log file directory.

All actions saved in log files can be replayed in the tool.

- To replay a log file, click Run ACE from the Script section of the File tab, and open a log file.

You can also replay a log file at the command line. To replay a saved log file, enter the following line at the command line:

<!-- formula-not-decoded -->

As the log file is read, all actions saved in the log file are performed in real time in the GUI.

## Viewing Command History

After you exit the tool, the underlying Tcl commands for all actions you take are saved to a log file.

## Running ACE Scripts

The Analysis Command Environment (ACE) is a Tcl-based programming environment comprised of a set of high-level waveform data operating commands evolved from the old Synopsys APX (Application Programming Extension) API functions. While the old APX API functions are still supported in ACE, the new high-level commands in ACE significantly increase the ease of use to construct scripts for complex analysis needs.

To run an ACE script, click Run ACE on the File tab.

The ACE commands support:

- Tcl list and Perl array variables for handling a collection of objects.
- Wild card name pattern for referencing multiple objects.
- Direct use of Tcl/Perl variables in waveform equations. All calculator functions are available for the sx\_equation command.
- Execution in both GUI mode and non-GUI batch mode.

## Supported File Formats

The following waveform formats are supported:

- Synopsys FSDB files (binary, v6.5 Linux platforms; v6.5 Windows platforms)
- Synopsys HSPICE® tr0, sw0, ac0, mt0, hb0, nw0, mc0, mct0, rlgc, wzo, annotate, listing file (Binary/ASCII)
- Synopsys StarSim™ wdb, wv, xp (binary)
- Synopsys HSIM®/NanoSim®/CustomSim™ wdb (binary)
- Synopsys HSIM/NanoSim out ,vector, .mt file (ASCII)
- Synopsys Saber AI/PL (binary/ASCII)
- Synopsys VCS®/Magellan™/DVE VPD (binary)
- Synopsys CustomSim .err, .errz, and .errt files

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

- Synopsys Galaxy Custom Compiler® Simulation and Analysis Environment (SAE) resultsMap.xml and results.xml files
- Cadence® Spectre® PSF, PSFXL (support only in Tran section for corners, MC, and sweeps), WSF (binary/ASCII), runObjFile
- Cadence PSPICE® DAT (binary), Allegro® SIM (ASCII)
- Verilog VCD (ASCII), ModelSim® WLF (binary)
- Mentor Graphics® ELDO®/ADMS™ COU, WDB (binary), AdiT TR0/TB0.
- SPICE3/SmartSpice raw format (binary/ASCII)
- Agilent® ADS .ds format (binary), TouchStone® S-parameters (ASCII)
- CSDF (Common Simulation Data Format) (ASCII)
- Text file, CSV (comma separated values) format
- Other in-house simulator formats (SDIF, MICS, TI-punch)
- Synopsys WDF format (binary)
- Binary scope data (Tektronix®, Agilent, Keysight, Teledyne Lecroy®)
- IBIS models, Synopsys Liberty® files

## Additional File Format Information

Additional information is available for the following file formats:

- Special Note for the ELDO COU Format
- Special Note for the ADMS/ELDO WDB Format
- Special Note for the PSF Format
- Special Note for the WDF, FSDB, Binary HSPICE tr0, and PSF Formats

## Special Note for the ELDO COU Format

The COU format from ELDO simulator can contain multiple simulation runs. Before loading a COU file, COU reader in the WaveView tool needs to scan the entire file to determine how many runs the COU file contains.

For very large COU files, the detection process might take a very long time because the reader has to sequentially examine all data in the COU files.

To speed up this COU file loading process, the WaveView tool has an alternative builtin search algorithm that can cut the file loading time significantly. To invoke the fast read option, set the SW\_SX\_FAST\_COU environment variable to any value in your shell (for example, setenv SW\_SX\_FAST\_COU ). Due to the nature of the COU format, the fast search algorithm has a trade-off that might potentially determine the number of runs of a COU file incorrectly. Although the possibility is very low, you can always disable the fast search algorithm by unsetting the environment variable (for example, unsetenv SW\_SX\_FAST\_COU ).

<!-- image -->

## Special Note for the ADMS/ELDO WDB Format

By default, a built-in WDB file reader is used to load data from WDB files generated by ADMS and ELDO. However, for small amount of simulation waveform data, the WDB writer in these simulators might buffer waveform data in the WDB Java server without writing them to a disk file. To work around this problem, you can take one of the following actions:

1. For ELDO, set the -isaving option to a smaller value to force more frequent incremental saving to disk files. The file size specified in the -isaving option is in MB. For ADMS, set the JwdbSpillThreshold option in $HOME/.vams\_setup to a smaller value to lower the buffer size.
2. Enter setenv SW\_SX\_JWDB\_API 1 at the command line to use the vendor-provided WDB API to load data directly from the Java WDB server. The API + Java WDB server operation, however, can be very slow for large WDB files.

## Special Note for the PSF Format

PSF format assigns a unit for each signal in a simulation output file. For noise analysis, to display different waveforms using proper scales, signals with V^2/Hz unit are automatically converted to V/sqrt(Hz) by taking the square root of the loaded value during the waveform loading process.

PrimeSim HSPICE splits large output PSF format data (&gt; 2GB) into multiple 2GB PSF files on 32-bit platform. Since 32-bit platform is obsolete and the simulator binary is always 64bit, there is no 2GB file size limitation for PSF file.

## Special Note for the WDF, FSDB, Binary HSPICE tr0, and PSF Formats

Split files are supported for the WDF, FSDB, binary HSPICE tr0, and PSF files. When these files are opened in the WaveView tool, a search is performed for the subsequent files in the same directory. For example, if the loaded file is output.wdf , the WaveView tool automatically looks for output.wdf.1 . If the output file is output.fsdb.1 , the WaveView tool looks for output.fsdb.2 . If you do not want to load the subsequent split files, disable the Automatically connect to subsequent split files option in the Loading Waveform Files dialog box.

## Opening a Waveform File

To open a waveform, click Open Waveform in the Waveform tab.

To abort loading a waveform file that is taking too long to load, click Abort Loading on the File tab.

## Opening Waveform Files in Case-Insensitive Mode

You can open waveform files in case-insensitive mode as follows:

- Using the command-line option -case\_insensitive\_mode
- Using the option -case\_insensitive with the ACE command sx\_open\_sim\_file\_read

For FSDB files, the tool does not perform a linear search, which provides significant performance improvement with the ACE command sx\_signal .

## Opening Multiple Files

If multiple files are loaded, to allow simultaneous signal browsing on these multiple target files, the Open New Browser context menu function opens multiple signal browsers for each waveform file respectively.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## Opening PWL Files

To open textual or PWL data, click Open Waveform on the File tab and expand the Additional PWL/Table Format Options section in the opened dialog box.

The WaveView tool supports data input in regular text format. Scaling factors (for example, 1ns) and scientific formats (for example, 1.0e-9) are both supported in the textual data files.

To distinguish WaveView text data files from regular text files, the first line of a text data file is reserved for the format specification and must appear in the following form, where format-type is the format type keyword:

#format format-type

Lines beginning with a number sign (#) are treated as comments.

## Note:

If the file cannot be recognized, use the option Force Open Waveform as to open the file as a SPICE PWL or text file.

<!-- image -->

The following sections describe how to prepare textual input for:

- Tabulated Data in Real Numbers
- Tabulated Data in Complex Numbers
- 2-Dimension Sweep Data in Real Numbers
- 2-Dimension Sweep Data in Complex Numbers
- Measured Data Without Name Header
- SPICE PWL Sources
- Opening Err Files

## Tabulated Data in Real Numbers

## Syntax:

```
#format table xvar signal1 signal2 .... valuex value1 value2 ... ...
```

xvar and signaln are variable names and valuen are numeric values. As a special-case exception, the first line can be omitted if the name of xvar is TIME .

## Example 1:

```
#format table VGATE Ichannel 0.0 0.0 1.0 1u 2.0 5u 3.0 5.2u ...
```

## Example 2:

The following data file can be recognized without the #format line:

```
TIME V(1) V(2) 0.0 5.0 2.5 1n 4.8 2.6 ...
```

If the data file does not contain the x-value column, (commonly seen in measurement data), add keyword #dataonly to the #format line. The reader automatically assigns a 0based row index as the x-axis value.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

If the signal names are embedded in the last '#' comment line before the actual waveform data values, add keyword #cmt\_name to the format line.

## Tabulated Data in Complex Numbers

Format for complex numbers in (real, imaginary) form.

## Syntax:

```
#format complex-ri xvar signal1 signal2 .... valuex value1-real value1-imag value2-real value2-imag ... ...
```

Format for complex numbers in (magnitude, angle [0-360]) form.

## Syntax:

```
#format complex-ma xvar signal1 signal2 .... valuex value1-mag value1-angle value2-mag value2-angle ... ...
```

Format for complex numbers in (magnitude, phase [0-2 ]) form:

## Syntax:

```
#format complex-mp xvar signal1 signal2 .... valuex value1-mag value1-phase value2-mag value2-phase ... ...
```

## Example:

```
#format complex-ri Freq vout 100meg 0.0 0.0 200meg 1.0 0.1 300meg 1.1 0.2 400meg 1.4 0.4 ...
```

## 2-Dimension Sweep Data in Real Numbers

## Syntax:

```
#format 2dsweep xvar2 xvar signal1 signal2 .... #sweep value1-x2 valuex value1 value2 ...
```

```
... #sweep value2-x2 valuex value1 value2 ... ...
```

where xvar2 is the name of the second sweep variable.

## Example:

```
#format 2dsweep vgs VDS Ichannel #sweep 0.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 1u 2.0 5u 3.0 5.2u #sweep 0.1 0.0 0.0 1.0 2u 2.0 6u 3.0 6.2u ...
```

## 2-Dimension Sweep Data in Complex Numbers

Format for complex numbers in (real, imaginary) form

## Syntax:

```
#format 2dsweep-ri xvar2 #sweep value1-x2 xvar signal1 signal2 .... valuex value1-real value1-imag value2-real value2-imag ... ... #sweep value2-x2 xvar signal1 signal2 .... valuex value1-real value1-imag value2-real value2-imag ... ...
```

Format for complex numbers in (magnitude, angle [0-360]) form.

## Syntax:

```
#format 2dsweep-ma xvar2 #sweep value1-x2 xvar signal1 signal2 .... valuex value1-real value1-imag value2-real value2-imag ... ... #sweep value2-x2 xvar signal1 signal2 ....
```

<!-- image -->

```
valuex value1-real value1-imag value2-real value2-imag ... ...
```

Format for complex numbers in (magnitude, phase [0-2 ]) form.

## Syntax:

```
#format 2dsweep-mp xvar2 #sweep value1-x2 xvar signal1 signal2 .... valuex value1-real value1-imag value2-real value2-imag ... ... #sweep value2-x2 xvar signal1 signal2 .... valuex value1-real value1-imag value2-real value2-imag ... ...
```

## Example:

```
#format 2dsweep-ma temp freq gain #sweep 50 100meg 1.0 0 200meg 1.0 90 300meg 1.1 120 400meg 1.4 150 #sweep 75 100meg 1.0 0 200meg 1.0 80 300meg 1.2 110 400meg 1.3 140 ...
```

## Measured Data Without Name Header

To import text measure data that does not have name header line or the x-axis value column, click Open Waveform and expand the Additional PWL/Table Format Options section.

Select the required options and click Ok to load the data file.

## SPICE PWL Sources

To import SPICE PWL sources into the WaveView tool, click Open Waveform and expand the Additional PWL/Table Format Options section.

Choose the SPICE PWL Source Data option and click Ok to load the data file. The SPICE PWL sources must not use any variable parameters.

<!-- image -->

## Opening Err Files

To open an .err file, click Open Err on the File tab. The errors are displayed in the .err File viewer dialog box.

## Opening RC Files

Setup files can be loaded from nWave (rc files) and Xelga (swd files). To load a setup file, click Load RC File in the File tab.

## Reading Compressed Waveform Files (Linux Only)

On Linux platforms only, compressed (.Z) or gzipped (.gz) waveform files can be directly opened in the WaveView tool. The tar.gz waveform files are not readable directly since a tar file can potentially contain multiple files.

By default the current working directory is used as the temporary directory to store the decompressed files. Decompressed files are automatically cleaned up when a the compressed file is closed in the WaveView tool. Set the SW\_SX\_TMP\_DIR environment variable to redirect the temporary directory to a different location.

## Working With WDF Files

The WDF (Waveform Data File) format is a Synopsys proprietary waveform storage format. The WDF format not only compresses analog and logic waveform data, it also facilitates fast waveform access for large data files. The compression scheme can be lossy or loss-less (default). Waveform data files in other formats can be converted into WDF files on demand.

The WDF format is directly supported by a number of simulators including HSIM, NanoSim, UltraSim, Spectre, and AMS-Designer.

You can extract signal files as a group. For example, you can create the following Tcl script file to extract signal files:

```
set f1 [sx_open_sim_file_read ./group.grp] sx_current_sim_file $f1 set sig [sx_signal x1] set sig2 [sx_signal x2] set f2 [sx_open_sim_file_write ./save2d.wdf] sx_save_signal $f2 "$sig $sig2" sx_close_sim_file $f2 sx_close_sim_file $f1
```

<!-- image -->

## Converting Waveform Files to WDF

To convert an open waveform file to WDF format, right-click the name of a waveform file name, and choose Convert to WDF from the menu that opens. The whole waveform file is saved into a new WDF file with X range you specify.

## Converting Existing Output Files to WDF

One or more output files can be converted (in batch mode) to Synopsys WDF files using the -c command-line option.

## Lossless Compression

With lossless compression, all original simulation output data points are preserved.

```
wv -c file1 file2 … filen
```

## Lossy Compression

You can use the -r command-line option to turn on data reduction for the compression process. Use -r 1 for moderate reduction or -r 2 for a more aggressive reduction.

```
wv -c -r (1 or 2) <-rv 0.001> <-ri 10n>
```

## Reducing WDF Data

The data reduction option removes redundant data points from straight waveform segments based on user-specified error tolerances. Data points are removed if the error between the original data points and the reduced PWL segments are smaller than the user-specified tolerance.

<!-- image -->

Figure 1 depicts the scheme used in WDF data reduction.

Figure 1 WDF data reduction scheme

<!-- image -->

The moderate reduction setting keeps at least 1 point out of four (4) original data points, while the more aggressive reduction mode keeps 1 out of ten (10) points. The -rv and -ri options are used to specify the reduction tolerance for voltage (or generic) waveforms and current waveforms respectively. The default setting is 5 mV for voltage waveform and 1 nA for current waveforms.

## Importing Multiple Files in Virtuoso

Parametric simulations in the Virtuoso environment can generate multiple output files in multiple directories. The locations and associated sweeping variables of these files can be found in the runObjFile log file.

The runObjFile can be opened directly in the WaveView tool to access these waveform files.

## Virtuoso dcOp Parametric Analysis

A dcOp analysis from a Virtuoso parametric run can also generate multiple result files. Each of these corner files contains a single-point operating point result for each device parameter. A special function is added in the Output View signal browser context menu to display or export these single-point values together with their sweeping variable conditions. Right-click a signal in the signal browser, and choose Signal 'NAME' &gt; Display Values or Signal 'NAME' &gt; Export Values .

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## Viewing the Waveform Hierarchy Browser

The Waveform Browser consists of an upper hierarchy browser and a lower signal list window. The lower list window displays signals under the selected hierarchy in the upper browser. Only one item can be selected in the upper hierarchy browser, while multiple signals can be selected in the signal windows for drag-and-drop operations.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

To distinguish waveform data with the same file names from different directories, in the root entries of the upper hierarchy browser, directory paths of loaded waveform files are displayed using directory prefix DX where X is the sequential index of different directories. To find out the original full paths of directory entries, select from the main menu File &gt; Show Directory Table to display the table that maps directory identifiers to full file paths.

<!-- image -->

## Displaying Signals

Signals from the Waveform Browser can be loaded into a waveview with the drag-anddrop operation. If a hierarchy (or file) entry is dragged from the upper hierarchy browser, all signals in the selected hierarchy level (or a file) are loaded. If a signal (or multiple signals) is dragged from the signal list window, only the selected signals are loaded. You can also double-click in the lower signal window to add an individual signal.

Depending on the signals being dragged, drop hints appear when signals are dragged over a waveview area. If the waveview is empty, hint boxes indicate available initial waveview modes. If the waveview contains existing panels, an insertion hint or drop-in box indicates the drop location.

If any signal from a waveform file is being displayed in a waveview window, the file icon changes, and the signal name is displayed in blue.

Alternatively, to plot all the signals of an instance, in the Waveform Browser, right-click an instance and select the Plot Waveform to option from the context menu.

## Pinning a Filter String

<!-- image -->

The toggle button pins or unpins a filter string to the current hierarchy. Once pinned (grey), the filter string is restored whenever selecting this hierarchy. The filter string is not editable while pinned. When unpinned (red), the filter string follows the preference of Keep Search String in the Signal List Filter .

<!-- image -->

## Viewing Filter History

Filter history allows you to select previous strings entered into the filter line editor. The history dynamically updates as text is entered, and appears as a drop-down when the line editor is focused. For example:

<!-- image -->

The history list includes the last ten strings. Click X to remove an individual string, click Clear Search String History to remove all strings, and press Esc to close the history list.

## Highlighting Waveforms

To highlight a waveform, click the signal check control button, and click the name of a signal to toggle its highlight state on and off.

You can also toggle a signal highlight by clicking the waveforms, which toggles the highlight states of all signals that intersect the mouse pointer.

To toggle which waveform is highlighted, press J to move down the waveform list and K to scroll up.

## Deleting Highlighted Waveforms

Right-click a highlighted signal and choose Cut from the signal context menu to delete all highlighted signals.

You can also move highlighted signals in a panel with a drag-and-drop operation. With the signal mode control button armed, follow the steps in Moving Panels or Copying Panels to move highlighted signals between panels or waveviews.

## Grouping and Ungrouping Highlighted Waveforms

Right-click a highlighted signal, and choose Group from the signal context menu to group all highlighted signals into a new panel.

You can also group signals by name by right-clicking signals and choosing Group By Name from the menu that opens.

To ungroup highlighted waveforms, right-click a highlighted signal, and choose Ungroup from the signal context menu to split each of the highlighted signals into a new panel.

<!-- image -->

## Copying Waveform Names

Right-click a highlighted signal, and choose Copy Label from the signal context menu to copy the names of all highlighted signals. This enables you to select and copy multiple signal names at one time. Note that the buffer size is limited to 8192.

## Sending a Waveform to Results Analyzer

Right-click a signal in the Waveform Browser or in the WaveView panel and choose Send to Results Analyzer to add signal expression/waveform from WaveView to Results Analyzer.

The RA calculator opens where you can construct or modify an expression.

## Grouping Waveform Files

Multiple waveform files can be collected into a group. When signals are loaded from a member in the grouped waveform files, the WaveView tool automatically loads the same signals from the other waveform files in the same group.

The grouping function is useful for loading signals from corner/alter simulations that usually involve multiple output files. To group multiple waveform files, right-click a waveform file, and choose File Grouping from the menu that opens. The Waveform Files Grouping window appears.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

Select waveform files in the list to group/ungroup them. For waveform formats that have associated sweeping parameters (such as the COU and the PSF format), click Select to filter files based on their parameter value conditions or by name of the .fsdb files.

The File Grouping function only ties multiple files into a group. It does not assign any parameter condition to each individual file. As a result, parametric analysis is not possible on these grouped files. To add corner parameter conditions to files, the files must be grouped into a file set using a link file (similar to the runObjFile approach). The link file not only specifies which files to be grouped, it also defines the associated parameter conditions for each file in the group. Grouped files using the link file are processed as a single file as if the result is from a sweep analysis. Since the link file provides sweeping parameter conditions, parametric analysis is also supported.

To create the link file, right-click a file name, and choose Create File Set from the menu that opens. To add parameter conditions to a file, enter the value in the (name=value) format, multiple values are delimited by comma (for example, temp=0,vdd=3.3). Click Add to add the parameter values to a file and the new values are indicated in the file list. Note that each of the files in a file set must have the same number of the same parameters. Finally, enter the path to the link file and click Ok to create the link file. Once a link file is generated, it can be opened directly as a regular waveform file.

If you want to update the plotted waveforms after files are added to or removed from a group, click the Update plots when adding/removing files to/from a group check box before clicking the Group or Ungrp buttons.

Bindkey for the File Grouping is available in the menu command.

## Bookmarking Waveform Files

A waveform file can be added to the bookmark list. Click Bookmarks and choose Manage Bookmarks in the File tab.

<!-- image -->

The Add/Manage Bookmarks window opens.

You can also reload a waveform file from the bookmark list from this window.

## Setting the Active Waveform File

To have all plotted signals come from a specified waveform file, right-click a waveform file name in the WaveForm Browser and select Set as Source of Plotted Signals .

## Updating Waveform Files

The WaveView tool can read growing waveform data files during a simulation job. Choose Update from the menu in the File section of the Waveform tab to update all displayed and derived signals.

If you restart a new simulation to override the old waveform data file, the update function automatically detects re-created data files and prompts you to select between keeping the old result or updating to new result.

If you keep the old data file, only the signals that are loaded are available from the old data file (because the old file is overwritten). An old data file is indicated by its blue file icon. To update an old data file to the new result, right-click the file in the Waveform Browser and choose Update WDF from the context menu.

To display signals from both the new and the old data file, choose to keep the old result. The old result file is saved and automatically opens the new data file.

If you need to update the WDF signal list, you can right-click the name of a file in the Waveform Browser and choose Reload WDF Signal List from the menu that appears.

## Printing Waveform Files

On Linux platforms, the WaveView tool supports printout in the PostScript format only. To submit a print job, choose Print from the menu in the File section of the Waveform tab open the Print Setup window.

The print target is defaulted to the current active waveview, which can be changed by clicking Change . Select your preferred settings and click Print to submit the print job.

## PostScript Print Layout

Multiple print options are supported for the PostScript printout:

- Print only the active waveview to a single page as shown on the screen.
- Print all signals in the active waveview using the display height. Multiple pages might be needed if the waveview has signals that are scrolled out of the view.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

- Print all waveviews in a single page, multi-column layout. The user can choose the number of columns preferred.
- Print all waveviews, each in a single page, as shown on the screen display.

Select the Color PostScript option if your printer supports color PostScript.

The default print setup is black/white in landscape orientation. The default printer device and user-defined print command can be predefined in the .spxrc file.

## Printing on Linux Platforms

On Linux platforms, the Print Setup dialog box supports print out to different paper sizes and printers. Printer names can be predefined in the Printer Devices field of the Preference Settings dialog box. Multiple printer names are delimited by semicolon (;). Selected paper size and printer device are saved in $HOME/.spxlast when the application is closed. The stored values are automatically used as the default when the application starts again. If the PRINTER environment variable is defined in your Linux shell, it is always used as the default printer.

## Printing on Windows Platforms

On MS Windows platforms, in additional to the PostScript print-to-file option, the WaveView tool also supports printout to all installed printers except line printers. PostScript format is supported as a file output option only. Choose Print from the menu in the File section of the Waveform tab to open the MS Windows version of the Print Setup dialog box. Select preferred options and click Continue to select a printer device, or select the path for the PostScript output file.

## Exporting Waveform Data

To export waveform data, choose Export from the menu in the File section of the Waveform tab. Enter your output path and other settings in the Waveform Export Parameters dialog.

Confirm your output file path to open the Waveform Export Parameters dialog box.

Choose the panels or waveviews you want to export in the Target section: Selected Panels , All Panels , Selected Waveviews , or All Waveviews . If you choose a selected panel or waveform option, you are prompted to choose those panels or waveviews once you click the OK button.

Also, choose which signal names you want to export in the Exported Signal Names section: Full Hierarchy or Net Name Only . Click Append File Name if you want to append the file name to the associated exported signals.

<!-- image -->

Waveform data in the active waveview can be saved using several different formats. The following formats are supported:

| Format     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Text Table | Tabulated format. You can specify output options in the Text Table Output Option section of the Waveform Export Parameters dialog box. Selecting the Suppress X-axis column option hides the x-axis in the table output. Selecting the Hex Logic Values option changes the binary logic output values to hexadecimal values. Selecting the Do not extend waveforms over the longer x-range of other waveforms option prevents waveforms from being extended over an x-range of another waveform that is longer.                                                                                                                                                            |
| PWL Source | SPICE PWL (piecewise linear) format. You can specify PWL logic levels and slew values in the Logic Waveforms to PWL Sources section, as well as any netlist syntax options in the PWL Source Netlist Syntax Options section of the Waveform Export Parameters dialog box.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| WDF        | Synopsys WDF compressed format. You can specify the Set Start X and Set Stop X values in the Text Table Output Option section of the Waveform Export Parameters dialog box.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| VCD        | VCD file with analog support. You can specify the VCD Timescale in the lower right-hand corner of the Waveform Export Parameters dialog box.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| M-File     | file. Choose the panels or waveviews you want to export in the Target section: Selected Panels , All Panels , Selected Waveviews , or All Waveviews . If you choose a selected panel or waveform option, you are prompted to choose those panels or waveviews once you click the OK button. Also, choose which signal names you want to export in the Exported Signal Names section: Full Hierarchy or Net Name Only . Click Append File Name if you want to append the file name to the associated exported signals. You can specify the Number of Valid Digits in the lower-left corner of the Waveform Export Parameters dialog box.                                    |
| FSDB       | FSDB file. Choose the panels or waveviews you want to export in the Target section: Selected Panels , All Panels , Selected Waveviews , or All Waveviews . If you choose a selected panel or waveform option, you are prompted to choose those panels or waveviews once you click the OK button. Also, choose which signal names you want to export in the Exported Signal Names section: Full Hierarchy or Net Name Only . Click Append File Name if you want to append the file name to the associated exported signals. You can specify the starting and stopping X values by clicking the Set X Start and Set Stop X options in the Text Table Output Options section. |

<!-- image -->

| Format   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|----------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| OUT      | .OUT file. Choose the panels or waveviews you want to export in the Target section: Selected Panels , All Panels , Selected Waveviews , or All Waveviews . If you choose a selected panel or waveform option, you are prompted to choose those panels or waveviews once you click the OK button. Also, choose which signal names you want to export in the Exported Signal Names section: Full Hierarchy or Net Name Only . Click Append File Name if you want to append the file name to the associated exported signals. You can specify the starting and stopping X values by clicking the Set X Start and Set Stop X options in the Text Table Output Options section. |

By default, the WaveView tool only exports waveforms in selected panels using the x-axis step of the very first signal. Click All Panels to export waveforms in all panels.

## Marching Waveforms

To automatically update waveforms from a running simulation job, choose Marching from the menu in the File section of the Waveform tab.

Enter the required update interval and the abort trial limit and click the Start button to start waveform marching. Automatic update is stopped if the waveform file is not growing after the retrial limit. The automatic update function can be manually stopped at any time by clicking the Stop button in the same dialog box.

If the automatic waveform marching is enabled, it is indicated with an icon in the main application toolbar.

## Saving and Loading SigLists

Signal list files include all signal names that are currently plotted.

To save a signal list file, click Save SigList from the menu in the File section of the Waveform tab.

To load a signal list file, click Load SigList from the menu in the File section of the Waveform tab. Click the Plot in current waveview check box to plot all signals in the current waveview; otherwise, all signals are plotted in a new waveview.

## Dumping the Screen

All waveforms in a waveview can be included when performing a screen dump, even if the waveforms are scrolled above or below the currently visible portion of the waveview window.

To include all off-screen waveforms, choose Dump Screen from the menu located in the File section of the Waveform tab. The Save Screen Dump dialog box opens. Click the Use Maximum WaveView Height check box, and click OK .

On Microsoft platforms, you can copy and paste the waveview contents to any application that has access to the clipboard. To copy the screen bitmap of a waveview window to the clipboard, choose Copy to Clipboard from the waveview context menu. To export a waveview in the vector-based Windows EMF (Enhanced Meta File) format, choose Screen Dump to EMF .

On Linux platforms, you can dump the waveview contents to either JPEG, PNG, BMP, or EMF formats. Choose Dump Screen from the waveview context menu to dump the display content.

To replace the special character that appears in the file name while dumping images, enable the Replace special char with check box, and enter the character of your choice. The special characters in the dumped file name are replaced with the entered character. For example, if the file name is a?1:2&lt;3 , and the number '5' is entered to replace the special characters, then the file name is updated as a515253 .

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## Dump All Screens

To dump all screens, choose Dump All Screens from the menu located in the File section of the Waveform tab. The Save Screen Dump dialog box opens.

## Setting Waveform Attributes

To modify waveform attributes for a waveform:

1. Double-click the signal name of the waveform, or click Settings on the Waveform tab, and choose Waveform Attributes from the menu that opens.

The Waveform Attributes dialog box opens with the attributes for the chosen signal.

2. Change any of the following waveform display attributes:
- Line Color
- Line Width
- Dash Type
- Marker Shape

3. For analog signals, change the following attributes as necessary:
- Display Preference
- Hide Signal
- Axis (left or right)
4. For digital signals, change the following attributes as necessary:
- Display Preference and type
- Mnemonic On
- Radix
5. For analog or digital signals, enter the marker frequency, which changes the display frequency of the data point markers.
6. (Optional) Click the Turn on Alias check box to change the alias of a signal.
7. Click Apply to save your changes.

## The Active Waveview

In the dock mode, the top waveview is considered the active waveview. In the undock mode, the top-most waveview or the selected waveview is the active waveview. Clicking the tab of a waveview window makes that waveview the active waveview.

## Adding a Waveview

An empty waveview is initially opened when the WaveView tool starts. To add more waveviews, click WaveView in the Add section of the Waveform tab.

<!-- image -->

The newly created waveview is placed on the top of the waveview stack.

## Deleting Waveviews

To delete the active waveview, click the X button of a waveview tab.

## Displaying WaveView Windows

A waveview window can have one or more non-overlapping Panels. Panels in a waveview can be arranged in two modes: vertical stack or independent row/column. In the vertical stack mode, panels stack top down and share a common horizontal axis. In the independent row/column mode, panels are arranged from left to right in a row. Panels in the row/column mode are independent of each other. A small icon at the upper-right corner of the waveview indicates the waveview orientation.

The following display modes are available:

- Stack Mode
- Row and Column Mode
- Vertical Row and Column Mode
- Horizontal Row and Column Mode
- Tiled Row and Column Mode
- TableView Mode

## Stack Mode

To view waveviews in vertical stack mode, right-click a waveview tab and choose Stack Layout from the menu that opens. Waveviews are displayed in this mode by default.

<!-- image -->

## The following figure shows the vertical layout display.

<!-- image -->

The vertical layout has the following display components:

- Control Buttons: Provides shortcuts to some of the commonly used waveview functions.
- Vertical Slider: Panes zoomed waveforms vertically. It is not displayed for logic panels.
- Vertical Axis: The vertical axis of a panel. For a logic panel, it displays the vector width and radix.
- Panel Slider: Panes the entire panel stack vertically when the waveview height is too small to show all panels. Mouse wheel can be used to scroll this slidebar.
- Horizontal Axis: The common x-axis of all panels, which appears at both the top and the bottom of a vertical waveview.
- Horizontal Slider: This slide bar is used to pane zoomed waves horizontally.
- Monitor Column: Displays waveform or cursor-related values. Multiple monitors can be added. A horizontal slide bar at the bottom scrolls long value strings horizontally.
- Monitor-Panel Divider: Defines the left boundary of the waveform plotting area. Click and drag over the divider to resize the width of monitor columns.
- Name-Monitor Divider: Defines the border between the name and monitor area. Click and drag the divider to resize the width of name and monitor columns.
- Name Column: Displays waveform names. A vertical slide bar scrolls name list vertically. A slide bar at the bottom scrolls long name strings horizontally.

<!-- image -->

## Row and Column Mode

To view waveviews in row and column mode, right-click a waveview tab and choose Row/ Column Layout from the menu that opens.

## Vertical Row and Column Mode

To view waveviews in vertical row and column mode, right-click a waveview tab and choose Single Column Layout from the menu that opens.

## Horizontal Row and Column Mode

To view waveviews in horizontal row and column mode, right-click a waveview tab and choose Single Row Layout from the menu that opens.

You can use the mouse to change the height and width of the Signal Name panel in Single Row Layout by hovering the mouse over the edges of the panel until the cursor becomes a double arrow, then clicking and dragging to adjust the size.

The following figure shows the independent row and column display.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

Panels in the independent row/column layout are arranged in a similar way to the Vertical Stack mode, except for the following differences and additional display components:

- Name column: The name column is located at the top of each panel. The vertical and horizontal slide bars can be used to scroll long list or long name strings.
- Monitor column: The monitor column is at the top of each panel. A horizontal slide bar at the bottom scrolls long value strings horizontally.
- Top Panel border: The top border can be moved to redefine the top boundary of the waveform plotting area. Drag the divider and move it vertically to resize name/monitor height.

Each waveview window is associated with a waveview context menu that can be invoked from the upper right corner of the window, or from the waveview tab area. Choose an item from the waveview context menu to rename, delete or refresh a waveview, or edit the waveview title.

## Tiled Row and Column Mode

To view waveviews in tiled row and column mode, right-click a waveview tab and choose Tile Row/Column Layout from the menu that opens.

## Synchronizing Waveviews

A stack-mode waveview can be synchronized with other stack-mode waveviews. Cursors and the x-axis of a synchronized waveview are updated automatically when the x-axis display range or the active cursor location changes in other synchronized waveviews. Right-click a waveview and choose Sync/Unsync from the menu that opens to toggle the sync state of the active waveview, or choose Sync/Unsync All to toggle the sync states of all waveviews.

## Toggling Sync Mode

<!-- image -->

The toggle button in the WaveView toolbar switches the synchronization status of the current waveview. When in sync mode ( ), clicking the button removes all panels in the current waveview from the sync group. When in unsync ( ), clicking the button adds all panels to the sync group.
