## Setting Filter Parameters

The following parameters are set from the Filter Settings tab in the Eye Diagram Settings window, which is used to exclude unwanted time periods when forming an eye diagram:

| Parameter Name   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| No Filter        | Specifies that no filter is enabled.                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Index Range      | Enables a filter for a specified index range. Enter values for the Starting Window Index and Number of Windows to select the range.                                                                                           |
| Time Range       | Enables a filter for a specified time range. Enter values for the Range Starting Time and Range Stopping Time .                                                                                                               |
| Skip Frequency   | Specifies the number of next trigger edges that are skipped. For example, if Skip Frequency is set to 2, the next 2 trigger edges will be skipped for a valid edge.                                                           |
| DDR 2/3T Mode    | Enables or disables the DDR 2/3T mode. When enabled, if the trigger edge is bigger clock+0.5*period, the edge is skipped. For example: set eye_obj [sx_create_eye $signal ui=auto trigger=ext trigsig=$strobe "option=ddr2t"] |
| All Bit Patterns | Shows all bit patterns.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Remove 0->X      | Filters out 0 to x transitions.                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Remove 1->X      | Filters out 1 to x transitions.                                                                                                                                                                                               |

|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

Cursors in a folded eye diagram trace the eye fuss (eye height/width) or the envelops of the eye pattern. Select the required Eye fuss values and envelop measurements from the cursor context menu. If a cursor is selected to trace the eye envelope, the cursor is automatically moved to its corresponding unfolded position when the eye diagram is unfolded. For more details, see Tracing Waveform Points in Eye Diagrams.

## Setting External Trigger Parameters

The External Trigger tab in the Eye Diagram Settings window specifies external trigger parameters only when external signals are set in the eye diagram panel.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

All signals and associated trigger values are displayed in the Trigger Signals table. You can change the trigger signal by dragging and dropping a new trigger into the table and clicking Apply .

## Generating Jitter Histograms

Cursors are normally used in Eye Diagrams to trace the eye envelope or fuss. They can be also used to produce jitter histograms from the eye envelope pattern. To create the jitter histograms, move a cursor and position its horizontal hair at a preferred level. Right-click a cursor, and choose View Histogram from the menu that opens.

The time (the offset into a folded eye window) is automatically sampled for each crosspoint between the horizontal hair and the eye waveform, and creates histograms for the two areas.

The generated histograms display the jitter distributions of the two cross section areas.

## Displaying the Eye Height Distribution

To display the vertical distribution values of the height of an eye as a histogram over the eye diagram:

1. Right-click an eye diagram, and choose Eye Height Distribution from the menu that opens.

The Eye Height Distribution dialog box opens.

2. Enter the X Value .

The eye height distribution begins with this x-axis value.

3. Click OK .

A histogram of vertical distribution values is displayed over the eye diagram.

## Adding User-Defined Masks

A mask is an abstract reference overlaid in eye diagrams to qualify signals timing integrity. Two built-in masks are provided: a standard mask for common near-end timing specifications and the IEEE802.3 mask. You can add your own mask definitions using mask files as well.

## Saving and Loading Masks

Use the Save Mask and Load Mask buttons of the Mask tab of the Eye-Diagram Settings dialog to save and load masks. This feature is supported for both standard and C-PHY masks.

Saved mask settings include all mask options shown on the Mask tab dialog. When saving a mask spec, you can choose to append the current mask setting to an existing file.

## Mask File Syntax

A mask file can contain one or multiple mask definitions. A mask consists of multiple segments that are lines plotted between adjacent points from a node list. Each mask definition is organized in the following format:

```
mask "maskname" direct|normalized "nodename", X, Y <newpath> "nodename", X, Y
```

…

The mask keyword starts a new mask definition, which must be followed by a quoted mask name and then a type keyword ( direct or normalized ) that specifies the mask type. The words mask , direct , normalized , and newpath are reserved keywords.

Each node in the list consists of a quoted node name, the X value of the node, and the Y value of the node. For a direct type mask, X is the X value into an eye window, and Y is the Y value of the node. For a normalized type mask, the X and Y values denote a node position as fractions into the eye window. X=0 (Y=0) is on the left (bottom) window edge and X=1 (Y=1) is on the right (top) window edge.

A newpath keyword breaks line strokes and starts a new drawing stroke.

## Incorporating Mask Files

The SW\_SX\_MASKFILE environment variable is used as a pointer to the user mask files.

To incorporate a mask file:

- On Linux Platforms

```
setenv SW_SX_MASKFILE file1:file2:filen
```

file1…filen are the path to the mask files. A column (:) is placed between file paths.

- On Windows 95/98 Platforms

Open a MSDOS window and edit AUTOEXEC.BAT in the top directory of your boot hard-drive (C:\, for example). Add the following line to the AUTOEXEC.BAT file:

```
SET SW_SX_MASKFILE=file1;file2;filen
```

The file names are separated by semicolumn (;) instead of column (:) because Windows uses column (:) as a drive delimiter.

- On Windows NT Platforms

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

Open the Control Panel and double-click the System icon. After you see the System Properties dialog box, select the Environment Variables tab. Add the SW\_SX\_MASKFILE environment variable.

- On Windows XP/2000 Platforms

Open the Control Panel and double-click the System icon. After you see the System Properties dialog box, click the Advanced tab and click the Environment Variables button. Add the SW\_SX\_MASKFILE environment variable.

- On Windows Me Platforms

Click Start , choose Run , then enter msconfig.exe and click OK to run the msconfig.exe program. Click the Environment tab and enter SW\_SX\_MASKFILE as a new environment variable. Make sure that the box before SW\_SX\_MASKFILE is checked to enable the environment variable.

These mask files are read at initialization time and the mask menu is expanded in the Eye Configuration dialog box with the user-defined masks.

## Mask File Example

The following mask example defines an IEEE802.3 mask as shown in the following figure.

<!-- image -->

```
mask "IEEE802.3" direct "A",  0.0n, 0.0 "C", 15.0n, 0.4 "D", 25.0n, 0.55 "E", 32.0n, 0.45 "F", 42.0n, 0.0 "G", 57.0n,-1.0 "T",110.0n,-1.0
```

```
"V",110.0n,-0.7 "S",111.0n,-0.15 "R",108.0n, 0.0 "Q",111.0n, 0.15 "P",110.0n, 0.75 "O",100.0n, 0.4 "N", 85.0n, 1.0 "B", 15.0n, 1.0 "A",  0.0n, 0.0 newpath "H", 48.0n, 0.7 "I", 67.0n, 0.6 "J", 92.0n, 0.0 "K", 74.0n,-0.55 "L", 73.0n,-0.55 "M", 58.0n, 0.0 "H", 48.0n, 0.7 newpath "U",100.0n,-0.3 "W", 90.0n,-0.7 "V",110.0n,-0.7 "U",100.0n,-0.3
```

## Logic Waveforms

A logic panel displays signals using digital timing diagram. It is permitted only in vertical stack waveviews. Logic panels accept signals that are represented in (time, logic) pairs. Various logic states including logic strength levels are supported. Zoom operation is supported along the x-axis direction.

Logic panels cannot be manually added from the application top menu. They are automatically created when logic signals are dropped into a vertical waveview.

Current vector width (number of bits) and radix setting of a logic panel are indicated in the left column of each panel (B: binary, O: octal, D: decimal, H: Hex-decimal, A: ASCII). The width digits are red color-coded for bus signals formed from originally separated bits, or yellow color-coded for a single bit extracted from an originally grouped bus signal.

Logic panels can be arbitrarily mixed with linear X-Y panels in a vertical stack waveview.

This section contains information on the following topics:

- Mnemonic Mapping for Bus Signals
- D to A Conversion

## Mnemonic Mapping for Bus Signals

Bus values can be mapped to predefined text strings. You can provide a translation table in an external file.

<!-- image -->

## Syntax:

```
# comment lines start with '#' value1 name1 value2 name2 …
```

The values are the bus values to be mapped.

The following formats are supported:

- 2400
- 0xAF32
- 'hAF32
- 'b1001\_0100\_0101
- 'd2400
- 'b110110111100
- 'o371

The names are the text strings to be mapped to. A text string must be quoted if the name contains spaces.

Wildcards are supported in Bus Mnemonic expressions. The ? character is a single bit for wildcards. It works only on 'b, 'o, and 'h.

## For example:

```
2'b1? 3'o1?1 4'h1?1?
```

You can load the translation table by clicking Settings in the Waveform tab and then choosing Bus Mnemonic Map from the menu that opens. Once a translation table is loaded, click Radix in the Panel section of the Waveform tab, and choose Mnemonic On/Off from the menu that opens to toggle the mapping settings.

The mapped values displayed in digital panel area is filled with color. This color is based on color information in map file.

## D to A Conversion

Logic waveforms can be converted into analog waveforms based on user-specified analog levels. D/A conversion can be applied only to waveforms in the logic panels.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

If the active waveview has only one panel, the D/A conversion operation is by default applied to all waveforms in this panel. If the active waveview has more than one panel, you need to select panels for the D/A conversion operation.

To open the D/A Conversion Parameters window, choose D to A from the menu located in the Utilities section of the Waveform tab.

Both single-bit and multi-bit D/A conversions are supported. Analog levels for multi-bit D/A conversion are determined based on rules. Enter the analog voltage levels for the low and high logic states.

There are two modes for D2A sampling: fixed rate sampling and value transition sampling. With the value transition sampling, the D-to-A conversion is completed only at the time when the input digital signal changes its value.

X and Z states can be converted to low or high voltage levels based on user preferences.

Click the Extend to Full Display Range button to extend the x-axis range to the current full x-axis display range for each converted analog waveforms, even if the original logic data has an x-axis range that is shorter than the full range.

You can also enable the Suffix of Result Signal Name option, which adds a suffix to the name of the converted signal name.

Rising and falling slews of the converted analog waveforms can be specified in the Preference Settings window (click Settings in the Configuration tab), or using the d2a\_rise\_slew and d2a\_fall\_slew configuration options.

## Tabular Panels

To create a new Tabular panel, choose Tabular from the menu in the Panel section of the Waveform tab.

See Working With Tableviews for more information on how to add a tableview and work with tabular panels.

## Histogram Panels

To create a histogram panel, an empty histogram panel must be created first by choosing Histogram from the menu in the Panel section of the Waveform tab.

Signals can then be dragged from the Waveform Browser and dropped into the histogram. Histogram panels can be placed only in horizontal waveviews.

A histogram plots an individual histogram for each signal in the panel. The average value and standard deviation can be annotated on top of each histogram and the number of bins and data bounds can be reconfigured. The WaveView tool can also calculate the distribution percentages of regions divided by user-defined markers from the histogram mean center.

<!-- image -->

## Configuring Histograms

To configure a histogram, right-click on the histogram panel and click Configure Histogram from the menu that opens. The Histogram Settings window opens.

Right-click on a histogram panel and click Export Histogram Measures to bring up a save file dialog for exporting the histogram measures. The m, s, RANGE, and BIN-Width values for the panel are saved in the specified file.

To change the maximum y-value in a histogram, open the Histogram Settings window and select the User-Defined Display Range check box. Enter the required maximum yvalue in the Display (Top) field.

<!-- image -->

The following settings are available:

| Setting           | Description                                                            |
|-------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Number of Bins    | The number of bins to display in the histogram.                        |
| Width of Bins (%) | The width of bins that can be set from 1% to 100%. The default is 99%. |

<!-- image -->

| Setting                                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|----------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Display Mode                           | The modes in which the histogram can be displayed. The following three display modes are provided: • Stack - The data of signals is stacked and displayed in histogram bins. • Side by Side - The data of signals is arranged side by side in histogram bins. • Overlap - The data of signals is overlapped on each other in histogram bins. |
| Show Average Line                      | Enables the average bar. The histogram is plotted by default.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Show a Single Histogram of All Signals | Plots a single histogram of all signals in a panel.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Y Value Normalized by Runs             | Normalizes the y-axis and sets it to the relative frequency (the number of occurrences divided by the number of Monte Carlo runs, for example).                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Show Normal Distribution Curve         | Displays the normal distribution curve over the histogram.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Show Density Estimation Curve          | Displays the density estimation curve over the histogram.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Find Distribution                      | Displays the data distributions for the following specified range in percentage units: • [beginning, mean - lower_marker*sigma] • (mean - lower_marker*sigma, mean] • (mean, mean+upper_marker*sigma] • (mean+upper_marker*sigma, ending]                                                                                                    |
| User-Defined Data Bounds               | Specifies the data range to be displayed, which is displayed as the x-axis range in a histogram panel.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| User-Defined Display Range             | Specifies the display range of a histogram panel. It is defined by left, right, and top (max. y-value) ranges.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

## Smith Chart

Smith charts display complex normalized impedance, admittance, and scattering parameters (S-parameters). To create a Smith chart panel, choose Smith Chart from the menu in the Panel section of the Waveform tab.

<!-- image -->

The Smith chart accepts signals that are represented in (real, complex) pairs. The normalized impedance is defaulted at 50 ohms and can be modified in Preference Settings (see the smith\_char\_impedance option in the .spxrc configuration file).

Smith charts are allowed only in horizontal waveviews.

You can configure a Smith chart by right-clicking a Smith chart and choosing Attributes from the menu that opens. The Smith Chart Settings dialog box opens.

Enter the required setting preferences and click OK to apply the changes.

Cursors (up to two) in a Smith chart can be used to trace the following value types:

- Gamma (the reflection coefficient)
- SWR (standing wave ratio)
- Impedance (Z)
- Admittance (Y)
- Frequency

You can change cursors by right-clicking on a Smith chart at the location where the cursor hairs cross, and one of these cursor types from the menu that opens

You can use the Data(X,Y) measurement to trace the frequency, magnitude, and phase values of a signal in a Smith chart.

The Zoom in and Zoom out buttons are used to zoom in and out a Smith chart. The Full Unzoom button displays a full-sized Smith chart.

## Polar Plot Panels

To create a new polar plot panel, choose Polar Plot from the menu in the Panel section of the Waveform tab.

Polar plots display data on a complex plane. They are allowed only in horizontal waveviews. The Polar plot accepts signals that are represented in (real, complex) pairs. The zoom operation is supported only along the radial direction.

## 2-D Sweeps

To create a new 2-D sweep panel, choose 2-D Sweep from the menu in the Panel section of the Waveform tab.

The 2-D Sweep panel displays 2-dimensional sweeping data on a flat X-Y plane. It is allowed only in horizontal waveviews. Similar to the 3-D Sweep panel, the 2-D Sweep panel accepts signals that are represented in ((x1, x2), value) pairs. Zoom operation is supported along both axes. Logarithmic scale is also supported along both axes (the x1 direction and the y direction, for example).

<!-- image -->

Both 2-D and 3-D sweep panels support sweep filters that display the selected sweep traces. Right-click a 2-D plot, and choose Sweep Line Filter from the menu that opens. You can highlight traces in the Sweep Line Filter dialog box that opens.

Enable the Display Trace Value option to display value label next to each sweep trace. If a 2D/3D sweep panel contains more than one signal, the first signal or the first highlighted signal is used as the filter target.

In 2-D sweep plot, the min/max Y-value bounds and the average Y-value of a multi-trace signal can be automatically extracted (for example, waveform envelop from statistical simulation result). To invoke this function, right-click a 2-D sweep panel, and choose Find Envelope Bound from the menu that opens. All data points are scanned from all traces, and three new waveforms representing the min/max bounds and the average waveform are created.

## Displaying Multi-trace Waveforms

A multi-trace signal contains multiple waveform traces. Each trace has a set of associated sweeping parameters (or sub X-variables). For example:

```
Trace 1: Temp=0 Vdd=3.3 Trace 2: Temp=0 Vdd=5 Trace 3: Temp=100 Vdd=3.3 Trace 3: Temp=100 Vdd=5
```

By default, a multi-trace signal is plotted with respect to its main independent sweeping variable (time, for example). In this case, the sweep line filter function in a 2D-sweep panel can used to selectively display some of the traces.

The 2D-sweep panel also supports plotting a multi-trace signal with respect to one of its sweeping parameters. To change the default X-axis of a 2D-sweep panel to a sub X-variable, right-click a 2-D panel, and choose Change X Variable from the menu that opens. Drag and drop a sweeping parameter from the Waveform Browser to the Setting X Variable dialog box. Choose Sweep Line Filter from the panel context menu to open the Sub X-Variable Plotting Filter dialog box.

## Note:

The filter setup is different between using the default x-axis and sub X-Variable x-axis. This is because in the sub X-Variable plot mode, based on the selected sub X-variable, the number of traces might vary depending on the number of unique combinations among other sweeping parameters. The number of traces are automatically detected and sorted in the order of the sub X-Variable values to display waveforms.

<!-- image -->

A multi-trace signal must have equal number of points in each of its original traces in order to be plotted in the sub X-variable mode.

Plotting a multi-trace signal with respect to another multi-trace signal is not supported.

## 3-D Sweeps

To create a new 3-D sweep panel, choose 3-D Sweep from the menu in the Panel section of the Waveform tab.

The 3-D Sweep panel displays 2-dimensional sweeping data on a 3-dimension coordinate. It is allowed only in horizontal waveviews. The 3-D Sweep panel accepts signals that are represented in ((x1, x2), value) pairs, where x1 and x2 are the first and second independent sweeping variable, respectively, and value can be either the value of a real signal or the magnitude/phase/real/imaginary part of a complex signal. The viewing angles of the 3-dimension coordinate can be interactively adjusted from the two sliders in the panel. The zoom operation is not supported. Logarithmic scale is supported only along the vertical axis.

## Pair Plot

To create a new pair plot, choose Pair Plot from the menu in the Panel section of the Waveform tab.

The pair plot displays measurement results in pairs for viewing Monte Carlo data correlation. It is allowed only in row/column waveviews.

The WaveView tool creates a table with a number of rows and columns equal to the number of signals plotted. Each cell/square represents a pair of plotted signals. The signals start from top to bottom, left to right.

Correlation coefficient (R) values are calculated for each pair. Pairs with a value of 0 are shown as white squares. Pairs with a value of 1.0 are shown as blue squares, while values between 0 and 1.0 are a lighter blue, growing darker the closer it is to 1.0. Pairs with a value of -1.0 are shown as red squares, while values between 0 and -1.0 are a lighter red, growing darker the closer it is to -1.0.

If a lot of signals are plotted, the squares are smaller and only the color is shown. The zoom operation is supported.

## For example:

<!-- image -->

When hovering the mouse over signal name, a yellow rectangle highlights the row containing the plotted signal. When hovering over a square cell, the tool shows the R value in a box with canvas background color, as well as the signal names in the y-axis and x-axis areas. When clicking on a square cell, the tool shows a scatter or histogram plot in a separate panel for further analysis. A new panel is created on the first click and reused on each subsequent click.

You can also add a cursor on Pair Plot panel, the R values for each signal is shown in monitor area.

## Constell Plot

This panel type supports optical and electrical constellations for OptSim simulations in OptoCompiler.

To create a new constellation, choose Constell Plot from the menu in the Panel section of the Waveform tab.

In this panel, you can plot regular, complex and sweep signals. The x-axis is the real part of the plotted signal and the y-axis is the imaginary part. You can also zoom in and zoom out in this panel.

<!-- image -->

- Plotting regular signals

For a regular non-complex signal, x-axis values are the signal values, and all y-axis values are equal to zero. The data points are drawn as markers in this panel.

- Plotting complex signals

For a complex signal, x-axis values are the real part of the signal and y-axis values are the imaginary part.

- Plotting sweep signals

For a sweep signal, each trace of the sweep signal is plotted as a regular/complex signal in this panel.

Figure 2 shows an example of a constell plot.

<!-- image -->

Figure 2 Constell plot

<!-- image -->

## Panel Set

A panel set is a named panel used for grouping signals from different panels. It can contain sublevel panel set panels. To create an empty panel set, choose Panel Set from the menu in the Panel section of the Waveform tab. It appears as follows:

<!-- image -->

When selecting to Delete , Cut , or Copy a panel set, the operation is applied to all panels contained in the panel set.

## Renaming a Panel Set

The name of a panel set is automatically assigned when created. To rename a panel set, right-click the panel and select Edit Label .

## Expanding a Panel Set

To expand or collapse all panels in a panel set, click the +/-icons before the panel set's name. When a panel is collapsed, meters located on that panel are hidden.

## Creating a Panel Set From Selected Panels

To create a panel set for selected panels, right-click a panel and select Create Panel Set . To ungroup all panels under one single panel set, right-click the panel and choose Ungroup Panel Set from the menu it opens.

To insert an empty panel set before a selected panel, right-click the panel and choose Insert Empty Panel Set .

<!-- image -->

## Rearranging Panel Set Panels

To move a panel out of a panel set, drag and drop that panel to after the last panel of the panel set, outside of the yellow bounding box. To move a panel to the end of a panel set, drag and drop that panel above the bottom of last panel, inside of the yellow bounding box.

## Parametric Plots

The following methods for generating parametric plots are available:

- Using the cursor in a 2D-sweep panel to plot the waveform value versus one of the sweeping parameters. Choose Plot Y vs. X2 from the cursor context menu. To select a sweeping parameter, right-click the waveform file of the signal in the Waveform Browser and choose X2 Parameter . This method is limited to displaying the waveform value only.
- Use the parametric() function in the equation builder. The parametric() function takes two arguments. The first argument must be a measurement of a multi-trace waveform; the second argument is the sweeping parameter to be used as the x-axis in the parametric plot (for example, parametric(mean("v(out)"),"TEMP" ). If the second argument is omitted, the default sweeping parameter is used.
- Use the built-in PrimeSim HSPICE parametric plot tool. The parametric tool only accepts HSPICE .MEASURE result files (.mtx/.msx/.max) as the input.

## Built-in Parametric Tool for PrimeSim HSPICE .ALTER Simulations

Choose Parametric Plot from the menu located in the Utilities section of the Waveform tab. Parametric plots directly from PrimeSim HSPICE measurement results files (.mt0/.ms0/.ma0 files) are supported.

The Parametric Plot tool can be used to generate scatter plot with measure result annotation. Select the X/Y parameters, the Scatter Plot option, and click Plot to create the scatter plot.

Generic parametric plot functions can be realized using the parametric() function in the equation builder.

## Plotting Clock Jitter

The built-in Jitter vs Time tool can be used to analyze clock jitter between any logic and analog target signal with respect to a reference signal. The reference signal can be an analog or logic signal from simulation output, or an idea signal defined using the width/

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

period/delay parameters. The jitter can be measure against the rise and fall edges of a reference signal.

To invoke the Jitter vs Time tool, choose Jitter vs. Time from the menu located in the Utilities section of the Waveform tab.

This section contains information on the following topics:

- Selecting Reference Signals
- Specifying the Target Signal
- Selecting Reference Edges
- Target Signal Edges
- Jitter Types
- Jitter Output Options

## Selecting Reference Signals

The reference signal can be selected from the following sources:

- User-defined Ideal Clock: An ideal clock signal defined by delay, period, and width.
- A Digital Signal: A digital simulation output waveform.
- An Analog Signal: An analog simulation output waveform.

The Digital or Analog Signal field requires an external waveform that can be specified in the External Signal field. Drag and drop the external signal from the Waveform Browser to the input field. If an analog reference signal is used, threshold value for the rise and fall edges also needs to be specified.

If the Display Reference Clock Signal option is selected, the reference signal is shown together with the jitter-versus-time output waveform.

## Specifying the Target Signal

The target signal can be either a digital or an analog simulation output waveform. The analog target waveform requires the rise/fall threshold values to be specified.

## Selecting Reference Edges

You can select the rise, fall, or both edges of the reference signal as the reference edge for the jitter evaluation.

## Target Signal Edges

The following options are available:

- Same as Reference : Finds rise-to-rise and fall-to-fall jitters.
- Rise : Finds jitter from reference edge to only the rising target edge.
- Fall : Finds jitter from reference edge to only the falling target edge.
- Cross : Finds jitter from reference edge to the next target switching edge (rise or fall).

The Target Signal Edge options are enabled only if the Jitter Type option is set to Trigger Time .

## Jitter Types

The Jitter vs. Time tool can evaluate jitter for the following types:

- Trigger Time : Measures the edge differences between the trigger edge and the signal edge.
- Pulse Width : Measures the pulse differences between the reference signal and the target signal at the reference edge.
- Period Width : Measures the period differences between the reference signal and the target signal at the reference edge.

By default, the target signal edges are searched in both directions from a reference switch edge. Select the Always Search Forward for Target Edge option to force the target search in the forward direction only.

The default target edge search range is half of the clock period at the current reference clock cycle. To limit the maximum search time range, enter the limit in the Max. Target Edge Search Range field.

## Jitter Output Options

The Jitter vs. Time result is displayed in a linear X-Y panel. PWL waveforms and bar charts are the available plot types. The jitter value sign can be selected between forwardpositive or backward-positive. In the forward positive mode, jitter values are positive if the target edge appears later than the reference edge.

<!-- image -->

## PrimeSim HSPICE QQ Plot

The PrimeSim HSPICE QQ statistical plot appears as follows:

<!-- image -->

After opening files, the measures are listed as signals in the output view.

When plotting QQ measure data, the WaveView tool displays it in an XY panel with Y2 Axis showed. The data array for each measure is used as x-axis and the quantiles array is used as y-axis. The quantiles array is global, which means all measures have the same Y values, but different X values.

The Y2 Axis shows the PNorm values of the standard normal quantile values. The fit line is plotted in the same panel. The Confidence interval lower and upper lines are plotted in the panel as well, as dashed lines.

When plotting QQ measurements, the tool does not share panels with other signals. Each QQ measure is in a new panel, along with fit line and confidence interval lines. Density bars are displayed in a new panel above the QQ measure plot panel.

Statistical summary information is displayed in a box in the bottom right corner of the panel.

When adding a cursor, the tool shows both left Y and right y-axis values for QQ plot lines, separated by the ; character.

The lower and upper specification limits are plotted as vertical red lines. If both lower and upper specification limits values are -Inf or Inf, there is no specification line displayed. If one of them is not -Inf or Inf, there is one vertical line displayed. If both of them are not -Inf or Inf value, there are two vertical lines displayed.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

If lower limit &lt; upper limit, a green bar is shown above the x-axis between lower limit and upper limit, with a red bar out side of [lower, upper] range. If lower limit &gt; upper limit, the tool shows a red bar above the x-axis between lower limit and upper limit, with a green bar out side of [lower, upper] range. If lower limit == upper limit, or both of them are -Inf or Inf value, the tool does not show bars.

## Searching Signals

The Signal Finder can be used to search signals from all (or selected) loaded waveform data files and hierarchies. Choose Signal Finder from the menu located in the Utilities section of the Waveform tab to open the Signal Finder dialog box.

<!-- image -->

The signal finder supports name patterns matching with the asterisk (*) and question mark (?) wildcards. Enter a search pattern and hit the return key or click Search button to commence a search. The search results are displayed in the right signal list window. Click a signal from the list window to highlight the signal source in the OutputView browser. Drag-and-drop operations are also supported from the signal finder result window into any waveview window. You can sort the results alphabetically by clicking the A-Z Sort and Z-A Sort buttons.

The search target signals can be refined to Voltage/Current signals only or All Signals by clicking one of the Type Filter option radio buttons. To limit the search to a file or a hierarchy level, select the corresponding entry from the left file/hierarchy browser. If the Selected Level Only option is selected, the target signals are those in the selected hierarchy/file only. If the Include Sub Levels option is selected, the target signals are those in and below the selected hierarchy/file.

<!-- image -->

On Linux platforms, select the Multiple Selection option to select multiple hierarchy entries as the search target.

The All and the None buttons are used to select/de-select all items in the right signal list window for the drag-and-drop operations.

Click Plot Overlap or Plot Stack to plot selected signals from the result window in overlap or stack mode.

The Case Sensitive option controls the signal name case sensitivity, while the Net Name Only and the Full Hier Name options control which part of the signal names to be used in the search process.

The Show Hierarchy , Show Filename , and Show Path+Filename options can be used to control the name appearance in the search result browser.

## Scanning Signals

Once signals are loaded onto a waveview, you can scan signals from the same files using the Scan control buttons. This feature can be used to compare signals from different data files.

Clicking the right arrow button advances signals from all selected panels to their corresponding next signals from the same waveform data files. Clicking the left arrow scans signals in the reverse direction.

Please note that scanning signals might require reloading data if the next/previous signals are not currently loaded. To speed up the scan process by avoiding data reloading, you might choose to load all waveform data to memory when waveform data files are initially opened (see Opening a Waveform File).

Default bindkey: N (next) or P (previous).

## Scan Settings

To change the scan settings, click Settings on the Waveform tab, and choose Scan Settings from the menu that opens.

You can configure the scan function into two different modes:

- Direct Scan : With the Direct mode, the WaveView tool scans signals according to their order in the waveform data file.
- Smart Scan : In the Smart mode, with a master waveform data file selected, the WaveView tool scans signals from the master waveform data file according to their order in the file, while automatically searches other waveform data files for signals with matched names.

<!-- image -->

Select a scan mode and a master file and click Apply to make the change. The Lock Scope option controls if the scan is limited within the current hierarchy scope.

## Data Reduction

To open the Data Reduction tool, choose Data Reduction from the menu located in the Utilities section of the Waveform tab. The Data Reduction Parameters dialog box appears, and the parameters are acquired for the data reduction operation.

Piecewise-linear waveforms often contain redundant data points. The data point reduction function allows users to remove redundant data points based on user-specified error tolerance. The same data reduction scheme is also used in WDF data reduction.

If the active waveview has only one panel, the reduction operation is by default applied to all waveforms in this panel. If the active waveview has more than one panel, you need to first select panels for the reduction operation.

Click Ok to start the data reduction operation. Waveforms with reduced data points are created in new panels in the same waveview.

## Direct Plot Mode

To enable direct plot mode, set WV\_DPLOT=1 , then click the following button at the top of the waveform browser:

<!-- image -->

Switching to direct plot mode changes the GUI as follows:

- The mini toolbar at the top of the Signal List is hidden.
- There is a new line editor for plotting:
- In the tree browser, the current file is selected and highlighted:

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

The following features are supported for searching:

- Full scope matching is supported using the delimiter . or /, based on the current file (the end of the delimited part represents the signal).
- Both * and ? are supported for scope and signal (* represents only one level).
- Multiple string searching is supported, separated by whitespace (for example, 'x1.x2.v* xx1.xx2.i*').
- Search results are shown in the Signal List with full scope name.
- Currently, search is insensitive and does not support regular expressions.

<!-- image -->

## Adding a Cursor

Cursors are used to trace waveform-related values. Multiple cursors can be added to a panel. The x-axis position of a cursor is indicated underneath the cursor hair.

To add a cursor, click Cursor in the Panel section of the Waveform tab, and choose Add Cursor from the menu that opens.

You can also click the cursor button in the button toolbar. Cursors can be added for delta measurements by pressing the left- and right-bracket keys ( [ and ] ) while moving the cursor.

When multiple cursors are added to a panel, the last moved or added cursor becomes the active cursor.

Waveform values corresponding to the active cursor are displayed in the monitor. In an XY panel, distances from all non-active cursors to the active cursor are displayed next to the active cursor.

If you want vertical cursor crossing points with the existing settings, in the Export VCursor Crossings dialog box, right click a vertical cursor, and choose Export V-Cursor Crossings With Existed Setting from the menu that opens. It exports the values without popping up the setup dialog box.

If you want to export Y values at specified X-value crossings to a text file, right-click a vertical cursor, and choose Export X-Values Crossings from the menu that opens.

If you want to export some or all vertical cursor crossing points to a text file, right-click a vertical cursor, and choose Export V-Cursor Crossings from the menu that opens. In the Target field, choose Selected Cursors or All Cursors .

If you want to export the Y value and data for logic signals in time sequence for all selected cursors, select multiple cursors, right-click on one cursor and select Export VCursor Crossings . All the values are exported to a file or text window.

This section contains information on the following topics:

- Selecting With the Cursor
- Active Cursor and Reference Cursor
- Moving a Cursor
- Showing and Hiding Distance Lines
- Setting Distance Between Two Cursors
- Locking Pairs of Cursors
- Locking Cursor Position

<!-- image -->

- Snapping the Cursor to an X/Y Value
- Snapping the Cursor to a Jump Type

## Selecting With the Cursor

The cursor is object-based and can select signals or panels, as follows:

- Mousing over a signal or panel highlights the object to be selected with a yellow box.
- Left-click selects the object. Ctrl-click and Shift-click can be used to select multiple objects at once. You cannot select both panels and signals at the same time.
- Right-click opens the context menu for the object (and select it if the object is not selected).
- When mousing over the naming area, the cursor appears as follows:
- For objects that can only be selected, the cursor is an arrow.
- For objects that can be expanded and collapsed, the cursor is a hand.

## Active Cursor and Reference Cursor

Distance lines are shown between a reference cursor and other cursors.

When you add, select, drag, or right-click a cursor, that cursor is set as the active cursor. The active cursor's value is displayed in the monitor.

The first added cursor is set as the reference cursor. The reference cursor can be different than the current cursor and does change when changing the current cursor. There can only be one reference cursor in an X-Y or logic panel. It is shown with a solid line. For example:

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

To set a cursor as the reference cursor, right-click the cursor and select Set as Reference Cursor . Or double-click a cursor and set the cursor as reference cursor in the Cursor Attributes dialog.

## Moving a Cursor

Depending on the default action of the left mouse button in a waveview (default left mouse button action can be specified in Left Button Default preference setting), a cursor can be moved with:

- Cursor Mode: If the left mouse button is pressed with mouse pointer near a cursor, the cursor is grabbed. A grabbed cursor can be dragged to a new position. If the mouse pointer is not in the vicinity of any cursor when the left mouse button is pressed, the active cursor is grabbed regardless of its position.
- Zoom-First Mode: If the left mouse button is pressed and released without any mouse pointer movement. The active cursor is grabbed to the mouse pointer location when the button is released.

In a zoomed panel, cursors outside the plotting range are placed on the left (or right) boundary of the plotting area. They can be grabbed from the borders of the plotting area. The cursor that is outside but closest to the boundary is grabbed first.

## Showing and Hiding Distance Lines

To show or hide the distance lines and delta value of a cursor, right-click the cursor and select Show/Hide Distance . Hiding distance on a reference cursor hides all distance lines.

When the preference Hide All Distance between Cursors is enabled, the tool hides all distance lines and value boxes for all cursors.

## Setting Distance Between Two Cursors

To set the distance between cursors, select two cursors, right-click on one of them and select Set Distance . Enter the required distance in the Cursor Distance dialog and click OK . The current cursor is moved to achieve the specified distance.

You can also open the Cursor Distance dialog by double-clicking on the distance value box or right-clicking on the distance value box and selecting Set Distance .

## Locking Pairs of Cursors

To lock a pair of cursors, select two cursors, right-click on one of them and select Lock distance .

You can also lock distance by enabling Lock Distance between Cursors in the Cursor Distance dialog.

To unlock distance, right-click on a cursor and select Unlock Distance .

To unlock a pair of locked cursors, choose Release Locked Pair from the context menu.

## Locking Cursor Position

To lock cursor position, enable Lock Cursor in the Set X-value and Set Y-value dialog boxes.

## Snapping the Cursor to an X/Y Value

To snap a vertical/horizontal cursor to an X/Y value, respectively, right-click on the cursor and select Set X/Y Value . Enter the required value in the dialog and click OK .

## Snapping the Cursor to a Jump Type

To snap the cursor to a jump type, perform the following steps:

1. Right-click on the added cursor, select Attributes . The Cursor Attributes dialog box opens.
2. Choose a Jump Type .

If you choose To , the cursor jumps to the X Value you have set in this field.

3. Select the Snap Cursor to Jump Type check box.

This snaps the cursor to the selected jump type.

4. Click OK

To enable or disable snapping the cursor to jump type, right-click on the added cursor, and select or deselect Snap Cursor to Jump Type to this position from the context- sensitive menu. When enabled, the cursor is snapped to the jump type position set in the earlier procedure.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## Setting the Cursor Alias Name

To set an alias name for a cursor, right-click on the cursor value label box and select Set Alias . Enter the alias name in the dialog and click OK .

## Showing and Hiding Cursor Crossing Values

Cursor value display has been enhanced as follows:

- Showing and hiding V-value crossings: To show/hide V-value crossing labels along a vertical cursor, right-click the cursor and select Show/Hide V-Value Crossings .
- Show/Hide X Value: To show/hide X-axis values crossing labels along a vertical cursor, right-click the cursor and select Show/Hide X Value . To set Hide X value as default, choose Configuration &gt; Preferences &gt; Waveview &gt; Waveview , select Hide X Values on the Value Labels at V-Cursor Crossing Points by Default .
- Showing and hiding H-value crossings: To show/hide H-value crossing labels along a horizontal cursor, right-click the cursor and select Show/Hide H-Value Crossings .

You can also choose to show signal names and file names of all plotted signals or (select signals) as detailed in the H-Cursor Attributes dialog.

- Showing P1/P2 and Delta Values: The tool shows crossing point values and delta values (P2-P1) of two crossing points between the reference cursor (P1) and the target cursor (P2). By default, the P1 value is shown along with the reference cursor, and the P2 value and delta value are shown along with the target cursor.

When distance lines are hidden, the delta value is not shown.

- When the preference Display Value Labels at Crossing Points by Default is enabled, the tool shows crossing labels along the cursor.
- The preference Show Reference Cursor Crossing Value can be set to the following:
- Individually - the P1 value is shown along the reference cursor and the P2 value and delta value are shown along the target cursor.
- Along with Target Cursor - the P1 value, P2 value, and delta value are all shown along with the target cursor.

## Cursors in Smith Charts and Polar Plots

In Smith charts and Polar plots, a cursor consists of a circle hair and a radial hair. The cross point is the cursor location and its value is displayed. A cursor can be grabbed by clicking the mouse button when the mouse pointer is near any of its two hairs. The cursor values in the monitor column trace the data points that are closest to the hair cross.

## Cursors in 2-D Sweep Panels

You can use a cursor in a 2D-sweep panel to create a new 'Y vs. X2' plot. Move the cursor to a preferred position, right-click the cursor, and choose Plot Y vs X2 from the menu that opens.

## Cursors in 3-D Sweep Panels

In a 3D-sweep panel, a cursor consists of a vertical hair, and two crossing hairs lying in the base plane. To grab a cursor in a 3D-sweep panel, move the mouse pointer near the vertical hair base where the two crossing hairs meet.

## Adding a Horizontal Cursor

Horizontal cursors are supported in analog X-Y panels. To add a horizontal cursor, click Cursor in the Panel section of the Waveform tab, and choose Add H-Cursor from the menu that opens.

You can also switch a vertical cursor to a horizontal cursor by right-clicking a vertical cursor and choosing Switch to H-Cursor from the menu that opens. The horizontal cursors trace the x-axis values of the nearest intersect point with waveforms. The x-values are displayed in the monitor column.

You can also click the Add Cursor control button to add an H-cursor by setting the Add H-Cursor with Add Cursor Control Button option in the preferences. To set this preference, click Settings in the Configuration tab, and click the WaveView tab. Click the Add H-Cursor with Add Cursor Control Button check box, and click OK .

This section contains information on the following topics:

- Annotating Horizontal Cursors
- Hiding Horizontal Cursors
- Anchoring Horizontal Cursors
- Exporting Horizontal Cursor Values

## Annotating Horizontal Cursors

In an X-Y panel, labels can be annotated to all the signal crossing points of a horizontal cursor. To enable crossing value labels, right-click an H-cursor, and choose Crossing Options from the cursor context menu.

## Note:

H-cursor label positions are recorded when the total number of H-crossing labels stay the same during H-cursor movement. The modified cursor label positions are saved in the session file.

<!-- image -->

## Hiding Horizontal Cursors

To hide the H-cursor hair, right-click an H-cursor, click the Hide Cursor Hair check box, and click OK .

## Anchoring Horizontal Cursors

To anchor horizontal cursors to a single panel, right-click an H-cursor, and choose Crossing Options from the menu that opens. Click the Cursor Anchor in Panel check box, and click OK

## Exporting Horizontal Cursor Values

If you want to export all horizontal cursor crossing points to a text file, right-click a vertical cursor, and choose Export H-Cursor Crossings from the menu that opens.

If you want to export X values at specified Y-value crossings to a text file, right-click a vertical cursor, and choose Export Y-Values Crossings from the menu that opens.

## Adding a Cross-Cursor

Cross-cursors are supported in analog X-Y panels. To add a cross-cursor, click Cursor in the Panel section of the Waveform tab, and choose Add Cross-Cursor from the menu that opens.

No monitor is created since there is only one crossing point for all waveforms. The cross-cursor has one vertical line and one horizontal line, showing X and Y values at the crossing point. The crossing point can be in different panels.

It appears as follows:

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

A cross-cursor has two modes:

- Floating (default) - the cursor can be placed at any location, and the vertical and horizontal line can both be moved individually and freely.
- Snap to waveform - when moving the vertical or horizontal line, the other line may be moved to snap to the waveform. It can be snapped to different waveforms. This is enabled by default.

You can set the X or Y value through the right-click Attributes dialog, the icon bar, or using jump forward/backward.

You can pair a cross-cursor with another cross-cursor, which shows the Delta X and Delta Y. For example:

<!-- image -->

## Jumping Forward and Backward

In an X-Y or logic panels, a cursor can be jumped forward to the next data point, peak, switching or crossing point using the cursor context menu.

To jump a cursor forward or backward, right-click near the cursor, and choose Jump (F)orward "SIGNAL" or Jump (B)ackward "SIGNAL" from the menu that opens to jump the cursor forward or backward on the target signal SIGNAL.

You can also select a cursor, then click Cursor in the Panel section of the Waveform tab, and choose Jump Forward or Jump Backward from the menu that opens.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

The target signal is indicated by a cross marker on the signal waveform at the intercept point with the cursor hair. To select a different target signal, move the cursor near a waveform (along the Y-direction) and the cross marker snaps to the new target waveform.

For digital panels, the cursor can be jumped to the next value change, the next match value, the next rise/fall edge, or the user-defined time.

To jump to a specific X value, right-click a V cursor, and choose Goto X Value from the menu that opens.

Default bindkeys: Press the F key to jump forward, and the B key to jump backward.

## Jump Settings

To change the jump parameters, click Cursor in the Panel section of the Waveform tab, and choose Jump Settings from the menu that opens to invoke the Cursor Jump Parameters dialog box.

Enter a preferred jump type and associated parameters and click Ok to make the change. Click Set as Default to save the settings in ~/.spxlast as the default setting.

## Deleting Cursors

To delete a single cursor, right-click near the cursor you want to delete, and choose Delete from the menu that opens to delete the cursor.

You can also select a cursor and click Cursor in the Panel section of the Waveform tab, and choose Delete Cursor from the menu that opens.

## Deleting All Cursors

To delete all cursors, select a group of cursors, and right-click near the selected group. Choose Delete All from the menu that opens to delete all cursors.

You can also select a group of cursors and click Cursor in the Panel section of the Waveform tab, and choose Delete All from the menu that opens.

## Assigning Cursors to Monitors

When you add a monitor of cursor value, if there is only one monitor, it links to the active cursor. Otherwise, the new added monitor links to a cursor that does not link to any monitor.

Selecting Auto Link Monitors from the monitor context menu links all monitors of cursor value to corresponding cursors.

<!-- image -->

Selecting Link to Monitor from the cursor context menu links selected cursors to corresponding monitors. If the tool cannot find a monitor for a selected cursor, it adds a new monitor and link it to this cursor.

## Using Cursor De-Select Mode

Disable the option Move Cursor to Mouse Click Position and the cursor operates in deselect mode and does not move.

## Using Monitors

Monitors are used to trace waveform-related values. Multiple monitors can be added to vertical waveviews, or panels in horizontal. The following monitors are available for analog panels:

| Monitor        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| cursor value   | (Y=) Traces waveform values that correspond to the current active cursor position. Logarithmic value is displayed if the corresponding panel has logarithmic Y-axis. To display the logarithmic value of a negative value x, the format -<log(abs(x))> is used. |
| derivative     | (S=) Traces waveform derivative values that correspond to the current active cursor position. Derivative of logarithmic values is displayed if the corresponding panel has logarithmic Y-axis.                                                                  |
| 1/derivative   | (1/S=) Traces the reciprocal of waveform derivative values that correspond to the current active cursor position.                                                                                                                                               |
| Y delta        | (D=) Displays difference between (1) waveform values that correspond to the active cursor position and (2) waveform values that correspond to the other cursor. Delta value is available only when a waveview (or panel) has two cursors.                       |
| cursor average | (A=) Displays waveform average between the cursors. Cursor average value is available only when a waveview (or panel) has two cursors.                                                                                                                          |
| maximum        | (MAX=) Displays waveform maximum values over full or zoomed signal range.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| minimum        | (MIN=) Displays waveform minimum values over full or zoomed signal range.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| peak-to-peak   | (PP=) Displays waveform peak-to-peak values over full or zoomed signal range.                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| average        | (AVG=) Displays waveform average values over full or zoomed signal range.                                                                                                                                                                                       |

<!-- image -->

| Monitor   | Description                                                                        |
|-----------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| RMS       | (RMS=) Displays waveform root mean square values over full or zoomed signal range. |

If you choose a maximum , minimum , peak-to-peak , average , or RMS monitor, you can also specify the following X-axis Range settings:

| X-Axis Range Option   | Description                                                                 |
|-----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| full signal range     | Measures across the full range of a signal.                                 |
| zoomed view range     | Measures just the zoomed portion of the signal that is currently displayed. |
| cursor range          | Measures between the x-values of two cursors.                               |
| user-defined range    | Measures between the two specified values.                                  |

This section contains information on the following topics:

- Adding Monitors
- Copying Monitor Values
- Reconfiguring Monitors
- Deleting Monitors
- Linking Monitors to Cursors
- Exporting Monitors

## Adding Monitors

To add a monitor, click Cursor in the Panel section of the Waveform tab, and choose Add Monitor from the menu that opens.

If a vertical waveview (or a panel in a horizontal waveview) has no existing monitor in the cursor value type, a cursor value type monitor is automatically added when a cursor is created.

When you add a monitor of cursor value, if there is only one monitor, it links to the active cursor. Otherwise, the new added monitor links to a cursor that does not link to any monitor.

<!-- image -->

To add a new monitor, click the control button to open the Monitor Settings dialog box. Select the preferred settings, and click Ok to create the monitor.

## Copying Monitor Values

To copy the value of a monitor, right-click a monitor, and choose Copy Value from the menu that opens. The value is copied to the clipboard.

## Reconfiguring Monitors

To reconfigure a monitor, right-click a monitor, and choose Configure Monitor from the menu that opens. In the Monitor Settings dialog box that opens, reconfigure the monitor, and click Ok to make the change.

## Deleting Monitors

To delete a monitor, right-click a monitor, and choose Delete Monitor from the menu that opens.

## Linking Monitors to Cursors

To link a monitor to a selected cursor, right-click a monitor and choose Link Cursor from the context menu that appears. In the Cursor Selection dialog box that opens, link any desired monitors to cursors.

## Exporting Monitors

To export monitors to a text or CSV file, right-click a monitor and choose Export Monitor from the context menu that appears. Choose an Output File name, Output Type , and Target in the Export Columns dialog box that opens, and click OK to export the monitors.

## Using the Measurement Tool

To access the Measurement Tool, click Measure Tool in the Utilities section of the Waveform tab.

Once one or more measurements are added to a waveview, you can drag those measurements to take the measurement interactively. If a panel has multiple signals and you want to perform a Width, Slew, Frequency, or Duty-Cycle measurement, the default measurement target is the first selected (highlighted) signal. The first signal is the default if no signal is selected.

## Note:

The names of any signals that are currently being measured are displayed at the bottom of measurement configuration dialog box.

This section contains information on the following topics:

- Setting the Measurement Font and Color
- Adding or Removing Measurement Favorites
- Viewing Measurement Results
- Setting the Precision of Measurements
- Exporting Measurements
- Locking and Unlocking Measurements

## Setting the Measurement Font and Color

You can set the font and color in the Measurement Tool window to label individual measurements to differentiate between measurements.

<!-- image -->

## Adding or Removing Measurement Favorites

In the Favorites tab of the Measurement Tool window, you can choose from several measurement you use most often.

To add a measurement to the list of favorites:

1. Click the All tab.

The available measurement categories and corresponding measurement appear.

2. Click a measurement.
3. Click the Favorite button at the bottom of the Measurement Tool window.

The selected measurement is saved as a favorite and is included as one of the measurements you can choose from the Favorite tab.

<!-- image -->

To remove a measurement from the favorite measurement list:

1. Click the Favorite tab.

The current measurement favorites are displayed at the top of the Measurement Tool window.

2. Click a measurement.
3. Click the Remove button at the bottom of the Measurement Tool window.

The selected measurement is removed from the list of favorite measurements you can choose from the Favorite tab.

## Viewing Measurement Results

To see existing Measurement Tool results from a waveview, right-click a measurement result in a waveview, and choose Measure Results from the menu that opens. The Measure Results window opens with a table of measurement result values.

## Setting the Precision of Measurements

To change the precision of measurements, click Settings in the Configuration tab, and then click the General category in the Settings Preferences window that opens. Enter a value in the Number of Valid Digits text box.

## Exporting Measurements

When you perform a measurement on a waveform, the measurement can be exported to the following equivalent forms:

- Equivalent PrimeSim HSPICE .MEASURE statements
- Tcl ACE sx\_equation statements
- Equation builder equations

To directly export a measurement to the Equation Builder, right-click a measurement and choose Measurement to Eqn from the context menu. The equivalent measurement equation and the result are displayed in the Equation Builder.

To export all measurements on a waveview window, right-click a measurement and choose Measurement Export . Use the Dynamic Measurement Export dialog box to select the measurements to be exported and the preferred export type. Only the following types of measurements can be exported:

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

- Rise/Fall time
- Width/Frequency
- Difference
- Y-Difference
- Y-Range

In the Dynamic Measurement Export dialog box, you can define the export name of individual measurements, enable or disable a measurement in the list, control how to count the number of switch edges, and define the precision for the exported values.

For PrimeSim HSPICE Measure and ACE Tcl export modes, the path of the output file must be specified.

## Locking and Unlocking Measurements

To lock or unlock a measurement, right-click the measurement and choose Lock Measurement or Unlock Measurement , respectively, from the menu that opens.

## Data(X,Y)

Displays the x-axis and y-axis values of a point on a waveform.

## Note:

This measurement is supported only in Analog X-Y, 2-D Sweep, and Smith Chart waveview panels.

The following parameters can be set for the Data(X,Y) measurement:

| Parameter                | Description                                                                                                                                                                          |

| All Signals              | Uses the min/max Y levels from all signals that are currently open. This option is only available when specifying a measurement Y level that is locked at a specified percentage.    |

| Range options            | • Entire Waveform -(default) measures the entire waveform. • Visible Range -measures the visible range. • User Specified -measures the defined range.                                |
| Label Move Independently | Allows label and endpoints to move independently.                                                                                                                                    |
| Label Move With Aim      | Allows label to move with the anchor marker.                                                                                                                                         |
| Show X-Axis Value        | Displays the x-axis value.                                                                                                                                                           |

## Delay

Calculates the delay between the edges of two waveforms relative to the default or specified topline and baseline levels for both the measured waveform and the reference waveform. The rising or falling edge on the reference waveform is assumed to cause the corresponding (rising or falling) edge on the measured waveform so that the reference edge occurs before the measured edge.

All rising or falling edges for the measured waveform are determined based on the Trigger setting in the Measure dialog box. From each edge, the corresponding previously occurring edge on the reference waveform is determined. The difference between the two edges on the x-axis is the delay time.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

The following parameters can be set for the Delay measurement:

| Parameter                                | Description                                                                                                                                                                        |
|------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Percentage                               | Locks the delay level at the specified percentages for the signal ( L(%) ) and reference signal ( Ref. L(%) ). In signal Y units.                                                  |
| Premise                                  | Specifies the delay value as either (default), positive delay, or negative delay.                                                                                                  |
| Signal Level                             | Locks the delay level at the specified levels for the signal ( L(V) ) and reference signal ( Ref. L(V) ). In signal Y units.                                                       |
| Target Signal                            | Uses the min/max Y levels from the signal you are currently measuring. This option is only available when specifying a delay level that is locked at a specified percentage range. |
| All Signals                              | Uses the min/max Y levels from all signals that are currently open. This option is only available when specifying a delay level that is locked at a specified percentage range.    |
| User Specified                           | Uses the min/max Y values you specify in the Min and Max text fields.                                                                                                              |
| Trigger                                  | Specifies the trigger type as Either , Rising , or Falling edge(s)                                                                                                                 |
| Ref. Trigger                             | Specifies the reference signal trigger type as Either , Same , or Opposite .                                                                                                       |
| Measure Between Closest Edges by Default | Finds the closest edge between the Signal and Ref. Signal .                                                                                                                        |
| Delay Rate vs. X-axis Plot Option        | Calculates the delay rate values of the Rise , Fall , or Rise/Fall edges vs. the x-axis.                                                                                           |
| Range options                            | • Entire Waveform -(default) measures the entire waveform. • Visible Range -measures the visible range. • User Specified -measures the defined range.                              |

## Jitter

Displays the histogram of crossing edges with a specified X range or Y range. You must click the right mouse button menu on the measurement to complete the measurement.

## Note:

This measurement is supported only in Analog X-Y, Eye Diagram, and 2-D Sweep waveview panels.

| All Signals     | Uses the min/max Y levels from all signals that are currently open. This option is only available when specifying a measurement Y level that is locked at a specified percentage.    |

## Settle Time

Calculates the settle time of a waveform with respect to a default or specified settle level and a specified settle band. The settle time is calculated by searching the waveform from right to left to find the first point that is outside of the settle band. The time that the waveform leaves the settle band is used as the settle time.

The following parameters can be set for the Settle Time measurement:

| Parameter       | Description                                                                                                                                                                         |
|-----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Percentage      | Locks the settle level at the specified percentage level ( Level(%) ). In signal Y units.                                                                                           |
| Signal Level    | Locks the settle level at the specified signal level ( Level(V) ). In signal Y units.                                                                                               |
| Target Signal   | Uses the min/max Y levels from the signal you are currently measuring. This option is only available when specifying a settle level that is locked at a specified percentage range. |
| All Signals     | Uses the min/max Y levels from all signals that are currently open. This option is only available when specifying a settle level that is locked at a specified percentage range.    |
| User Specified  | Uses the min/max Y values you specify in the Min and Max text fields.                                                                                                               |
| %of SettleLevel | Calculates the band value as the specified band value percentage multiplied by the settle level (for example, 5*settle_level).                                                      |
| %of PeaktoPeak  | Calculates the band value as the specified band value percentage multiplied by the peak to peak range of the signal (for example, 5*peak_to_peak_range).                            |
| Absolute        | Calculates the band value as the specified value (in signal Y units).                                                                                                               |

## Slew Rate

Calculates the slew rate of a waveform relative to the default or specified topline and baseline levels.

## Note:

This measurement is only supported in Analog X-Y waveview panels.

The slew rate is calculated using the difference between the upper and lower levels of a waveform divided by the risetime or falltime of the edge. You can select the upper and lower levels as a percentage of the topline or baseline.

| Target Signal                    | Uses the min/max Y levels from the signal you are currently measuring. This option is only available when specifying a rise/fall margin that is locked at a specified percentage range. |
| All Signals                      | Uses the min/max Y levels from all signals that are currently open. This option is only available when specifying a rise/fall margin that is locked at a specified percentage range.    |
| User Specified                   | Uses the min/max Y values you specify in the Min and Max text fields.                                                                                                                   |
| Slew Rate vs. X-axis Plot Option | Calculates the slew rate values of the Rise , Fall , or Rise/Fall edges vs. the x-axis.                                                                                                 |

## Highpass

Calculates the corner frequency of a waveform with a highpass shape. The highpass measurement is calculated relative to a default offset or a specified topline and a specified offset.

<!-- image -->

The corner frequency is calculated by searching from the right to the left until the waveform first falls below the measurement level, which is determined by the specified offset value (from the topline).

The following parameters can be set for the Highpass measurement:

| Parameter                | Description                                                                                                                                                                    |
|--------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Percentage               | Locks the topline at the specified percentage ( Topline(%) ). In signal Y units.                                                                                               |
| Signal Level             | Locks the topline at the specified signal level (Topline). In signal Y units.                                                                                                  |
| Auto Detect              | Calculates the topline and uses that value.                                                                                                                                    |
| Target Signal            | Uses the min/max Y levels from the signal you are currently measuring. This option is only available when specifying a topline that is locked at a specified percentage range. |
| All Signals              | Uses the min/max Y levels from all signals that are currently open. This option is only available when specifying a topline that is locked at a specified percentage range.    |
| User Specified           | Uses the min/max Y values you specify in the Min and Max text fields.                                                                                                          |
| Offset                   | Specifies the offset in Y-axis units.                                                                                                                                          |
| Show Topline             | Displays the topline.                                                                                                                                                          |
| Show Topline+Offset Line | Shows the cross line in a panel.                                                                                                                                               |

## Stopband

Calculates the stopband, low, high, or center frequency level or the level at which the measurement is calculated for a stopband-shaped waveform. This measurement is calculated relative to a default or specified topline level and a specified offset:

```
fcenter = square root of (flow*fhigh) quality factor = fcenter/bandwidth
```
