## delay

Calculates the time difference between two signals by the edge index and at the specified switching edges.

## Syntax

```
delay(<trigger_signal>,<target_signal>,<trigger_y_level>, <target_y_level>,<trigger_x_index>,<target_x_index>, [<trigger_x_start>],[<percent>],[<target_x_start>], [<target_start_relative_to>],[<x_stop>], [<trigger_edge_type>],[<target_edge_type>], [<trigger_periodicity>],[<target_periodicity>], [<trigger_tolerance>],[<target_tolerance>], [<occurrences>],[<output_xaxistype>],[<premise>])
```

<!-- image -->

## Returns

```
An analog scalar value. Arguments <trigger_signal> The reference signal. <target_signal> The signal to be calculated. Analog signals are supported. <trigger_y_level> The y_threshold for the trigger signal. <target_y_level> The y_threshold for the target signal. <trigger_x_index> The index value for the trigger signal. <target_x_index> The index value for the target signal. [<trigger_x_start>] The time value on the x-axis (the start time for the trigger signal). [<percent>] (Optional) The percentage value, which can only be 0 or 1 . If specified as 1 , the y_level is considered a percentage value; if not, Y is 0 . [<target_x_start>] The start time for the target signal. [<target_start_relative_to>] Specifies whether the start time for the target signal is relative to the trigger signal start time or time. [<x_stop>] The stop time for the target signal. [<trigger_edge_type>] The edge type of the crossing for the trigger signal. There are three options: rising, falling, or either.
```

<!-- image -->

```
delay('0|v(out)','0|v(out)',3,2,2,6,2n,0)
```

<!-- image -->

Chapter 7: Supported Functions Measurement Functions [&lt;target\_edge\_type&gt;] The edge type of the crossing for the target signal. There are three options: rising, falling, or either. [&lt;trigger\_periodicity&gt;] The periodic interval for the trigger signal. The delay algorithm for multiple occurrences returns the difference between the X points for the specified edges on the target and trigger waveforms (with the specified periodicity). For example, if the edge number specified for both waveforms is 1 and periodicity is 2, then it computes the difference between the 1,3,5,7... edges for both the waveforms. [&lt;target\_periodicity&gt;] The periodic interval for the target signal. [&lt;trigger\_tolerance&gt;] The tolerance value to detect the threshold crossings for the trigger signal. [&lt;target\_tolerance&gt;] The tolerance value to detect the threshold crossings for the target signal. [&lt;occurrences&gt;] Specifies whether you want to retrieve only one occurrence of a delay time event ( single ), or all occurrences of delay time events ( multiple ). The default is single . [&lt;output\_xaxistype&gt;] Specifies whether you want to output the delay time data against the trigger time, target time, or cycle. Cycle numbers refer to the nth occurrence of the delay time. This option is valid only when [&lt;occurrences&gt;] is set to multiple . [&lt;premise&gt;] Specifies the delay value as positive , negative , or either . Errors Possible error messages include: · Signal not found · (Target/Trig)Y value out of range Examples delay('0|v(out)','0|v(out)',3,2,2,6,0)

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## The arguments are as follows:

- Trigger Signal 0|v(in1)
- Target Signal 0|v(signal1)
- Trigger Y level - Y level threshold of the trigger signal, equal to 1 in this case.
- Target Y level - Y level threshold of the target signal, equal to 1 in this case.
- Trigger X index - The edge index of the trigger signal. In this case, the delay is calculated on the second index of the trigger signal.
- Target X index - The edge index of the target signal. In this case, the delay is calculated between the second index of the target signal and the second index of the trigger signal.
- Trigger X start - The start x-value of the trigger signal.
- Target X start - The start x-value of the target signal.
- X stop - X-value stop times for both trigger and target signals.
- Trigger edge type - The edge type of the trigger signal. It is rise in this case.
- Target edge type - The edge type of the target signal. In this case, it is the opposite of the trigger signal edge type, and therefore it is false.

## enb

Calculates the effective number of bits of a given signal. The FFT is calculated first, then the SNDR. The formula is ENB=(SNDR-1.76)/6.02.

## Syntax

```
enb(<signal>,<x_start>,<x_stop>,<num_of_points>, <signal_freq>,[<band_limit>],[<windowing_type>], [<decimation_rate>]), [<bin_size>],[<window_alpha>],[<normalization>],[<user_defined_value>],[ <suppress_dc>],[<dual_sideband>],[<max_harmonic_index>],[include_floor_no ise],[<full_scale>])
```

## Returns

An analog scalar value.

## Arguments

```
<signal> The signal to be calculated. <x_start> The starting point of X in the given signal. <x_stop> The stopping point of X in the given signal. <num_of_points> The number of points needing to be measured. <signal_freq> The frequency of an input signal. [<band_limit>] (Optional) Sets the band limit frequency of the signal. [<windowing_type>] Specifies the windowing function. The default is rectangle .
```

```
[<decimation_rate>] Specifies the decimation rate, which is the process of reducing the sampling rate
```

a signal. Normally, this argument is an integer or a rational fraction greater than one dividing the sampling rate.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

[&lt;bin\_size&gt;] (Optional) For window sampling, the bin\_size parameter is required to include all neighboring components within +/- bin size spectral range as part of the original fundamental (or harmonic) components. Default bin size is 10. [&lt;window\_alpha&gt;] (Optional) Windowing alpha is only applicable for Kaiser, Kaiser-bessel, and Gaussian window types. Accepts values from 1.0 to 20.0. The default is 3.0. [&lt;normalization&gt;] (Optional) There are three options for this argument:

- None - FFT results are not normalized.
- Normalized - FFT results are normalized against the maximum magnitude value of the waveform.
- User-defined - FFT results are normalized against a user-defined magnitude value.

[&lt;user\_defined\_value&gt;] (Optional) This argument is only applicable if [&lt;normalization&gt;] is set to userdefined. [&lt;suppress\_dc&gt;] (Optional) If set to true, the DC component is excluded from the target waveforms in the FFT/DFT operation. This is to minimize the error introduced by those signals with large DC component and very small AC magnitudes. [&lt;dual\_sideband&gt;] (Optional) If this argument is set to false, the resultant waveform is only on one side of the Y-axis starting from 0 to N-1. When set to true, the resultant waveform is symmetric to the Y-axis from -N/2 to N/2. [&lt;max\_harmonic\_index&gt;] (Optional) The harmonic index of the maximum harmonic component. [&lt;include\_floor\_noise&gt;] (Optional) If set to true, floor noise components are counted in calculation. [&lt;full\_scale&gt;] (Optional) If set to true, the magnitude of fundamental component is scaled to 1.

And the formula is changed to ENB=(SNR-1.76)/6.02.

## Errors

Possible error messages include:

- Signal not found
- Invalid input value
- X value out of range
- Number of sample points is non-positive
- Number of sample points is not power of 2

## Examples

enb('0|v(out)',0,8n,1024,100M,deci=20)

## flatten

## Description

Flattens the specified signal with a specified parameter as the new x-axis. The flatten function can be used if you have a set of sweep scalar values that you want to process further using calculator functions that take a signal as an argument. The flatten function is particularly useful when you have single point analyses (DC, AC) over a parametric sweep or corners and you want to convert the result into a suitable form for calculator function measurements.

## Syntax

```
flatten (signal <string>, param name <string>) Arguments signal The signal to flatten. param name (Optional) The parameter to become the x-axis.
```

## ipn

Calculates the n-order intercept point between the target signal and reference signal.For a non-linear system with an output and two fundamental excitation f1 and f2 frequencies, the nth order Intercept Point is the point on a set of PowerOut ( PowerOut1 and PowerOutn ) versus PowerIn curves at which a line extrapolated from PowerOut1 with a slope of 1 and a line with a slope of n extrapolated from the PowerOutn intersect. PowerOut1 represents the first order term, and PowerOutn is the nth order term. Both lines must be extrapolated from a region with sufficiently low input power. OIPn is the value of PowerOut at which IPn occurs. IIPn is the value of the PowerIn value at which IPn occurs.

<!-- image -->

## Syntax

```
ipn(<signal>,<reference_signal>,<term_order>, <extrapolation_point>,[<input|output>]) Returns An analog scalar value. Arguments <signal> The signal to be calculated. Analog signals are supported. <reference_signal> The reference signal. <term_order> An integer value, which can be 0 , 1 , ... , or n . n is the slope of the linear function. <extrapolation_point> The extrapolated X value at which two signals start to intercept each other. [<input|output>] (Optional) The X and Y components on the waveform, where X is the input and Y is the output . The default is output .
```

## Errors

Possible error messages include:

- Signal not found
- X value out of range

## Examples

```
ipn('0|v(out)','0|v(out)',3,4n) ipn('0|v(out)','0|v(out)',3,4n,'input')
```

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## measure\_eyejitter

Calculates Crossing Average, Crossing StdDev, Random Jitter (left), Random Jitter (right), and Deterministic Jitter of a signal using Eye Diagram.

## Syntax

measure\_eyejitter(&lt;eye\_object&gt;,&lt;vref&gt;,&lt;return\_type&gt;)

## Returns

A scalar value

## Arguments

&lt;eye\_object&gt;

The output of the create\_eye function.

&lt;vref&gt;

The threshold reference voltage level at which the crossing points are measured.

```
[<return_type>]
```

(Optional) The returned measurement type, which includes enumerated values in a list of all the measurements that the eye jitter measurement function returns.

The following values are included:

- CrossingAverage: Measures the average of the crossing times at the threshold level.
- CrossingStdDev: Measures StdDev of the crossing times at the threshold level.
- RandomJitter (left): Measures the Random Jitter at the left side of eye crossings.
- RandomJitter (right): Measures the Random Jitter at the right side of eye crossings.
- DeterministicJitter: Measures the time difference between the peaks of eye crossings on the left side and right side.

Deterministic and Random Jitter are calculated using the histograms of crossing times. If a deterministic jitter is present, each side of the distribution is expected to have two peaks. As shown in the following image, the crossing times on the left of the eye open are sampled into the histogram in red, and the crossing times on the right of the eye open are sampled into the histogram in green. The density estimation curves for both histograms are calculated. Deterministic Jitter is the distance between the two peeks of the curve. For the red histogram, it is P2-P1 and same for the green one. The Total Deterministic Jitter is calculated by the average of the Deterministic Jitter of red and green.

Random Jitter is the standard deviation of the distribution. It is calculated by:

<!-- image -->

Where, μ is the mean, x is the x-value from B1 marker to P1 marker (in red histogram, tail of the distribution) and p is the corresponding height. The same calculation is repeated for the other tail from B2 to P2. Random Jitter (left) is the average stddev of the two tails. Random Jitter (right) is calculated in the same way on the green histogram.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## Errors

Possible error messages include:

- Reference voltage is not specified
- Signal must be eye object
- No valid eye object

[n=<nth_index>] (Optional) The integer number. Specifies the index of edge to be measured. It , the function

## pam4\_ser

Measures the symbol-error rate (SER) for PAM4 electrical signals

## Expression Field

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## Syntax

```
pam4_ser(<signal>,[<x_start>],[<x_stop>], [<num_of_points>],[<result_type>], [<symbol_rate>],[<num_pre-symbols>], [<num_post-symbols>],[<dec_optimization>], [<dec-pt_shift_tol>],[<min_dec-pt_shift>], [<max_dec-pt_shift>],[<dec-pt_shift>], [<dec-level_selection>],[<first_dec_level>], [<second_dec_level>],[<third_dec_level>], [<num_ISI_symbols>])
```

## Note:

There is a difference between signal name specification in PrimeWave vs. standalone WaveView usage. The examples in the proceeding sections demonstrate the use of both the syntax without detailed explanation. For more information and examples, see Differences Between PrimeWave Expression Syntax and Standalone WaveView Expression Syntax.

<!-- image -->

## Description

This function measures the symbol-error rate (SER) for PAM4 electrical signals, taking an analog electrical PAM4 signal as input and estimating the rate of symbol errors from the signal's eye diagram.

You can define the number of symbols at the start and end of the input signal to be excluded from the SER algorithm. This approach is helpful when you want to avoid including numerical transient effects or discontinuities in the calculation.

The SER is calculated by constructing histograms for each of the four PAM4 symbol levels in the eye diagram, from which estimates are made for the mean and standard-deviation values for each symbol at a particular decision time relative to the center of the eye. An SER is then estimated in each case, assuming Gaussian noise distributions. A final SER is then calculated based on the SER for each symbol.

You can specify whether the decision time used for the SER calculation should be optimized by sweeping over a specified range of values, or whether a fixed value should be used. If a sweep is selected, you can adjust the tolerance for the search, as well as adjust the minimum and maximum shift values.

As for the three decision thresholds used to recognize the four PAM4 symbols, the user can specify that they be automatically set based on the optical modulation amplitude of the signal ( OMSouter ) and the average signal level Pave [1]:

<!-- formula-not-decoded -->

Alternatively, you can choose to specify these values directly.

You can also account for the effects of inter-symbol interference by calculating SER values for different partial eyes representing different symbol patterns. You should specify a value for num\_ISI\_Symbols &gt; 0, in which case SER values are calculated for the center symbol of each possible symbol pattern of length 2. num\_ISI\_Symbols +1. The final SER is calculated as a weighted average of these values.

Finally, the pam4\_ser() function provides the facility to measure and report values for not just the SER, but also the final decision-time shift and OMAouter .

## Arguments

&lt;signal&gt;

- The analog PAM4 signal to be calculated.
- Valid signal types: analog single-trace waveform or multiple-trace waveform, expression.

<!-- image -->

- Invalid signal types: digital signal, scalar value.
- When the y values of the trace are complex numbers, the magnitude is automatically applied.

```
[<x_start>]
```

(Optional) The starting point of x. The default is the beginning of the signal.

```
[<x_stop>]
```

(Optional) The ending point of x. The default is the end of the signal.

```
[<num_of_points>]
```

- (Optional) The number of points needing to be measured.
- Algorithm adjusts the signal sampling and time interval such that the number of data points is the closest power of 2 greater than or equal to &lt;num\_of\_points&gt;, and the number of symbols is the closest power of 2 less than or equal to the total number of symbols in the time interval.
- The default is the number of points in the requested time interval.

```
[<result_type>]
```

(Optional) Specifies the measurement value to produce. Default is ser .

- ser - the SER value
- decisionPointShift - the decision-time shift relative to the eye center used for the final SER value
- omaOuter - outer modulation amplitude (OMA)
- (Optional) Symbol rate of signal.
- Must be positive. The default is 26.5625e9.
- (Optional) Number of initial symbols to ignore.
- Must be greater than or equal to 0. The default is 0.
- (Optional) Number of final symbols to ignore.
- Must be greater than or equal to 0. The default is 0.

```
[<symbol_rate>]
```

```
[<num_pre-symbols>]
```

```
[<num_post-symbols>]
```

```
[<dec_optimization>]
```

(Optional) Specifies how to optimize the decision time. Default is sweep .

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

- sweep - sweeps the decision-point shift relative to the eye center time to find the best SER
- none - uses the user-specified decision-point shift
- (Optional) Tolerance for decision-point time-shift optimization.
- Must be greater than 0. Default is 1e-3.
- (Optional) Minimum decision point shift, specified as a fraction of a symbol period.
- Must be in the interval (-0.5,0.5). The default -0.05.

```
[<dec-pt_shift_tolerance>]
```

```
[<min_dec-pt_shift>]
```

```
[<max_dec-pt_shift>]
```

(Optional) Maximum decision-point shift, specified as a fraction of a symbol period. Must be in the interval (-0.5,0.5). The default 0.05.

```
[<dec-pt_shift>]
```

- (Optional) User-specified decision-point shift, specified as a fraction of a symbol period.
- Must be in the interval (-0.5,0.5). The default is 0.

```
[<dec-level_selection>] (Optional) Specifies how to determine decision thresholds. Default is oma . · oma - based on OMAouter calculated from an eye diagram · defined - uses user-specified decision thresholds [<first_dec_level>] (Optional) User-specified first decision threshold. Default is 0. [<second_dec_level>] (Optional) User-specified second decision threshold. Default is 0. [<third_dec_level>] (Optional) User-specified third decision threshold. Default is 0. [<num_ISI_Symbols]>] (Optional) Specifies additional symbols to account for ISI.
```

## Returns

- When the given signal is a single-trace waveform, this function returns a scalar value of a specified result type.
- When the given signal is a multiple-trace waveform, this function returns a waveform of a specified result type.

## Errors

The possible error messages include:

- Signal not found
- Number of sample points is non-positive
- Number of symbols is non-positive
- Symbol rate is non-positive
- Number of pre-symbols is negative
- Number of post-symbols is positive
- Invalid decision-shift tolerance
- Invalid decision-shift minimum
- Invalid decision-shift maximum
- Logic signals not supported
- Complex signals not supported
- End time is outside waveform range
- Signal must be analog
- SER calculation failure

<!-- image -->

## Examples

## Input Signal Waveform:

<!-- image -->

## Expression Field:

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## PrimeWave Expression:

```
pam4_ser(v(/net3),0,308.5n,524288,ser,53.125e9,2,4,none, decisionPointShift=0,decisionLevelSelection=oma)
```

## Standalone WaveView Expression:

```
pam4_ser('v(net3)',0,308.5n,524288,ser,53.125e9,2,4,none, decisionPointShift=0,decisionLevelSelection=oma)
```

45.5783m

If specified as 1 , the y_level is considered a percentage value; if not, Y is 0 . [<edge_index>] (Optional) The index of the edge. The default value is 1 . [<min>] (Optional) Min value for percentage y init/final. Default is xmin or ymin depending on type. ## root

- In case of nth\_root &lt;0, return value is the maximum value of x at which f(x) equals the specified threshold.

## settling\_t

## Description

Measures the settling time of given signal. Settling time is the time required for the response curve to reach and stay within a range of certain percentage (usually 5% or 2% of the final value).

Figure 3 settling\_t Example

<!-- image -->

## To calculate the d value:

d=(yvalue at xstop - yvalue at xstart)*settle\_band%

If half\_band\_error=false , the signal is considered settled when the y values of the signals are within (yvalue at xstop+(d/2) and (yvalue at xstop-(d/2) , and the tool reports the xvalue(time) at which this signal entered into this range of settling time.

If half\_band\_error=true , the signal is considered settled when the y values of the signals are within (yvalue at xstop+(d) and (yvalue at xstop-(d) , and tool reports the xvalue(time) at which this signal entered into this range of settling time.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

```
Syntax settling_t(<signal>,<start>,<stop>,<settle_band>,[<x_end>],[start_by =x/y],[stop_by=x/y],[<half_error_band>], [<occurrences>],[<output_xaxistype>]) Returns An analog scalar value. Arguments <signal> The signal to be measured. <start> The starting value. <stop> The stopping value. <settle_band> A percentage value. For example, to set the settle band to 3%, set this value to 3 . This is equivalent to the d value in Figure 3. [<x_end>] (Optional) The ending value of X. If <x_end> is specified, the function calculates the settle time in a sub-window waveform. [<start_by>] (Optional) The starting value, which can be X or Y. If you specify start_by='x' , the starting value is for the x-axis (the x-start value in Figure 3). If you specify start_by='y' , the starting value is for the y-axis (the L value in Figure 3). The default value is x . [<stop_by>] (Optional) The stopping value, which can be X or Y. If you specify stop_by='x' , the stopping value is for the x-axis (the x-stop value in Figure 3). If you specify stop_by='y' , the stopping value is for the y-axis (the H value in Figure 3). The default value is 'x' . [<half_error_band>] (Optional) If half_error_band is false (the default), the signal should settle between H +( d /2) and H -( d /2). If half_error_band is true, the user-defined settle_band value is equal to half of the error band. In that case, the signal should settle between H + d & H -d .
```

```
[<occurrences>]
```

Specifies whether you want to retrieve only one occurrence of a settling time event (single), or all occurrences of settling time (multiple). The default value is single.

```
[<output_xaxistype>]
```

Specifies whether you want to output settling time data against time or cycle. Cycle numbers is the nth occurrence of the setting time event in the input waveform. This option is valid only when [&lt;occurrences&gt;] is set to 'multiple'.

## Errors

Possible error messages include:

- Signal not found
- Y value out of range
- X value out of range

## Examples

```
settling_t('x|clip(v(refpad1),0,20n)',1.4,1.8,settle_band=1,xend=15n,star t_by='y',stop_by='y')
```

In this example, first d value is calculated as (1.8-1.4)*1%=0.004 .

Therefore, the signal can be considered settled when the y values of the signals are within 1.8+0.004=1.8004 and 1.8-0.004=1.7996 , and tool will report the xvalue(time) at which this signal entered in to this range as settling time. Here, since xend=15n , the tool will not consider the second glitch because it appears after 15n.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

settling\_t('x|clip(v(refpad1),0,20n)',1.4,1.8,1,start\_by='y',stop\_by='y')

In this example, there is no xend value defined, so the tool considers the entire signal (up to 20n) for the settling time. Because there is a glitch occurring around 17n, the settling happens after the glitch.

<!-- image -->

## sfdr

## Description

Measures the spurious free dynamic range. SFDR is the strength ratio of the fundamental signal to the strongest spurious signal in the specified frequency band set by the Start and End frequency fields.

or:

when the full\_scale option is true.

## Syntax

```
sfdr(<signal>,<x_start>,<x_stop>,<num_of_points>, <signal_freq>,[<band_limit>],[<windowing_type>], [<decimation_rate>],[<bin_size>], [<window_alpha>],[<normalization>], [<user_defined_value>],[<suppress_dc>], [<dual_sideband>],[<max_harmonic_index>],[<include floor noise>],[<full_scale>])
```

## Arguments

&lt;signal&gt;

The signal to be measured.

&lt;x\_start&gt;

The starting value of x.

&lt;x\_stop&gt;

The stopping value of x.

&lt;num\_of\_points&gt;

The number of points needing to be measured.

&lt;signal\_freq&gt;

The input signal frequency.

```
[<band_limit>]
```

(Optional) The limit band frequency to be set.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

```
[<windowing_type>] (Optional) Specifies the windowing function. The default is rectangle. [<decimation_rate>] Specifies the decimation rate, which is the process of reducing the sampling rate a signal. Normally, this argument is an integer or a rational fraction greater than one dividing the sampling rate. [<bin_size>] (Optional) For window sampling, the bin_size parameter is required to include all neighboring components within +/- bin size spectral range as part of the original fundamental (or harmonic) components. Default bin size is 10. [<window_alpha>] (Optional) Windowing alpha is only applicable for Kaiser, Kaiser-bessel, and Gaussian window types. [<normalization>] (Optional) There are three options for this argument: · none - FFT results are not normalized. · normalized - FFT results are normalized against the maximum magnitude value of the waveform. · user-defined - FFT results are normalized against a user-defined magnitude value. [<user_defined_value>] (Optional) This argument is only applicable if [<normalization>] is set to userdefined. [<suppress_dc>] (Optional) If set to true, the DC component is excluded from the target waveforms in the FFT/DFT operation. This is to minimize the error introduced by those signals with large DC component and very small AC magnitudes. [<dual_sideband>] (Optional) If this argument is set to false, the resultant waveform is only on one side of the Y-axis starting from 0 to N-1. When set to true, the resultant waveform is symmetric to the Y-axis from -N/2 to N/2. [<max_harmonic_index>] (Optional) The harmonic index of the maximum harmonic component.
```

Measurement Functions

```
[<include floor noise>] (Optional) When enabled, the sfdr function takes spurs from harmonics and noise. [<full_scale>] (Optional) If set to true, the magnitude of fundamental component is scaled to 1.
```

## Errors

Possible error messages include:

- Signal not found
- Invalid input value
- X value out of range
- Number of sample points is non-positive
- Number of sample points is not power of 2

## Examples

```
sfdr('0|v(out)',2n,4n,1024,500M) sfdr('0|v(out)',2n,4n,1024,500M,550M,'rectangle',deci=2)
```

(Optional) If this argument is set to false, the resultant waveform is only on one side of the Y-axis starting from 0 to N-1. When set to true, the resultant waveform is symmetric to the Y-axis from -N/2 to N/2.

```
[<max_harmonic_index>]
```

(Optional) The harmonic index of the maximum harmonic component.

```
[<include_floor_noise>]
```

(Optional) If set to true, floor noise components are counted in SNR calculation.

<!-- formula-not-decoded -->

(Optional) If set to true, the magnitude of fundamental component is scaled to 1.

```
[<window_sampling>]
```

(Optional) Determines whether the window samples are computed in a periodic or symmetric manner. For example, when set to periodic, the window extends by 1 sample. The default is symmetric.

## Errors

Possible error messages include:

- Signal not found
- Invalid input value
- X value out of range
- Number of sample points is non-positive
- Number of sample points is not power of 2

## Examples

```
snr('0|v(out)',4n,8n,1024,750M) snr('0|v(out)',4n,8n,1024,750M,10G,deci=20)
```

## snr\_f

Measures the signal-to-noise ratio of a given signal (in dB units), which is the resulting waveform of a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) signal. A similar algorithm with SNR.

V1 is the signal component in the range between signal\_from and signal\_to ; V2... V n are the noise components in the range of noise\_from and noise\_to .

<!-- image -->

## Syntax

```
snr_f(<signal>,<signal_from>,<signal_to>,<noise_from>, <noise_to>)
```

## Returns

An analog scalar value.

## Arguments

```
<signal>
```

The signal to be measured.

```
<signal_from>
```

The starting point of signal around harmonic.

```
<signal_to>
```

The stopping point of signal around harmonic.

```
<noise_from>
```

The point where noise begins.

```
<noise_to>
```

The point where noise stops.

```
[<window_sampling>]
```

(Optional) Determines whether the window samples are computed in a periodic or symmetric manner. For example, when set to periodic, the window extends by 1 sample. The default is symmetric.

## Errors

Possible error messages include:

- Signal not found
- Invalid input value

## Examples

```
snr_f('0|v(out)',75M,80M,100m,10G)
```

## snrh

Measures the Noise floor/rtHZ in support of spectrum measurements.

<!-- image -->

## Syntax

```
snrh(<signal>,<x_start>,<x_stop>,<num_of_points>, <signal_freq>,[<band_limit>],[<windowing_type>], [<decimation_rate>]),[<bin_size>],[<window_alpha>], [<normalization>],[<user_defined_value>],[<suppress_dc>], [<dual_sideband>],[<max_harmonic_index>],[include_floor_noise], [<full_scale>]) Returns An analog scalar value. Arguments <signal> The signal to be measured. <x_start> The starting value of x. <x_stop> The stopping value of x. <num_of_points> The number of points needing to be measured. <signal_freq> The input signal frequency. [<band_limit>] (Optional) The limit band frequency to be set. [<windowing_type>] Specifies the windowing function. The default is rectangle. [<decimation rate>] Specifies the decimation rate, which is the process of reducing the sampling rate a signal. This argument is usually an integer or a rational fraction greater than one dividing the sample rate. [<bin_size>] (Optional) For window sampling, the bin_size parameter is required to include all neighboring components within +/- bin size spectral range as part of the original fundamental (or harmonic) components. Default bin size is 10.
```

<!-- image -->

```
[<window_alpha>]
```

(Optional) Windowing alpha is only applicable for Kaiser, Kaiser-bessel, and Gaussian window types. Accepts values from 1.0 to 20.0. The default is 3.0.

```
[<normalization>]
```

(Optional) There are three options for this argument:

- None - FFT results are not normalized.
- Normalized - FFT results are normalized against the maximum magnitude value of the waveform.
- User-defined - FFT results are normalized against a user-defined magnitude value.

```
[<user_defined_value>]
```

(Optional) This argument is only applicable if normalization is set to userdefined.

```
[<suppress_dc>]
```

(Optional) If set to true, the DC component is excluded from the target waveforms in the FFT/DFT operation. This is to minimize the error introduced by those signals with large DC component and very small AC magnitudes.

[&lt;dual\_sideband&gt;]

(Optional) If this argument is set to false, the resultant waveform is only on one side of the Y-axis starting from 0 to N-1. When set to true, the resultant waveform is symmetric to the Y-axis from -N/2 to N/2.

[&lt;max\_harmonic\_index&gt;]

(Optional) The harmonic index of the maximum harmonic component.

[&lt;include\_floor\_noise&gt;]

(Optional) If set to true, floor noise components are counted in SNR calculation.

[&lt;full\_scale&gt;]

(Optional) If set to true, the magnitude of fundamental component is scaled to 1.

## yield

Measures the count of the value specified by spec\_min and spec\_max and returns the value for (valid\_count/total\_count)*100.

Where,

total\_count = total number of input data point count

valid\_count = total\_count - invalid\_count

If spec\_min is defined and any one data point in the input (signal/measurement) &lt; spec\_min, or if spec\_max is defined and the value &gt; spec\_max, then it is an invalid\_count.

Also all NaN values and errors are viewed as invalid\_count.

## Syntax

yield(signal&lt;string&gt;,spec\_min&lt;string&gt;,spec\_max&lt;string&gt;)

## Arguments

signal

The signal or measurement to be calculated.

```
spec_min
```

(Optional) The minimum spec value.

<!-- image -->

```
spec_max
```

(Optional) The maximum spec value.

## yvalue

Measures the y value of a given signal at x.

## Syntax

```
yvalue(<signal/scalar>,<x_value>,[<method>], [<occurrences>],[<period>],[<output_xAxisType>],[<extrapolate>])
```

## Returns

An analog scalar value.

<!-- image -->

## Arguments

```
<signal> The signal to be measured. <x_value> The input x value. [<method>] (Optional) Specifies the interpolation method. The default is linear. If set to round_down , the point value is the lower bound of an interval that contained it. [<occurrences>] (Optional) Specifies the result to be only one occurrence of an interpolated value for the given waveform ( single ) or all interpolated values for the given waveform ( multiple ), which you can later plot or print. The default is single . [<period>] (Optional) Specifies the time interval to calculate the next Y value. [<output_xAxisType>] (Optional) Specifies the X axis type of the result waveform. The value can be x or idx . [<extrapolate>] (Optional) When enabled, ignores the boundary and always returns a value. Errors Possible error messages include: · Signal not found · X value out of range Examples yvalue('0|v(out)',2n)
```

## Waveform Functions

This topic contains information on how to use the supported waveform functions.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

The following sections summarize the waveform functions available in the Calculator. Waveform functions must operate on waveforms (or derived waveforms). They always return new waveforms.

| Function      | Description                                                                                                                                           |
|---------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| a2d           | Converts the input signal from analog to digital.                                                                                                     |
| average       | Calculates the running average waveform of a given signal in the specified range.                                                                     |
| bestfit       | Measures the best fit line for a waveform.                                                                                                            |
| clip          | Generates a new waveform whose x range is limited to the given x_start and x_stop values. The y range is limited to the given y_min and y_max values. |
| concat        | Concatenates up to 32 signals or scalar values into one signal. The result signal's x-axis values are data point indixes.                             |
| cPwrContour   | Generates contours with the same power for Z-Smith.                                                                                                   |
| create_bus    | Creates a bus signal with given name and up to 31 digital signals.                                                                                    |
| create_eye    | Creates an eye object which can be plotted as an eye diagram.                                                                                         |
| crossings     | Calculates the crossing points between signal1 and signal2 or a given ylevel value.                                                                   |
| d2a           | Converts the input signal from digital to analog.                                                                                                     |
| dBc2V2        | Converts phase noise signal from dBc/Hz to V^2/Hz. Only works for waveform files that contain carrier magnitude information.                          |
| dBCPVRICurves | Creates a signal associated with an nth compression point measurement.                                                                                |
| delayvst      | Measures the time difference versus the time between two signals at the specified switching edges from x_start to x_stop.                             |
| derivative    | Calculates the derivative waveform of given signal.                                                                                                   |
| dft           | Measures the Fast-Fourier-Transform (FFT) of a given signal. The signal is evenly Piece-Wise-Constant sampled from x_start to x_stop for n points.    |
| dftbb         | Computes the fast Fourier transform (FFT) of a complex signal.                                                                                        |
| dnl           | Computes the differential non-linearity of a transient simple or parametric waveform.                                                                 |
| dumpPWLF      | Saves the signal to a text file for PWLF sources.                                                                                                     |
| duty_vs_t     | Measures the duty cycle versus time.                                                                                                                  |

<!-- image -->

| Function            | Description                                                                                                                                        |
|---------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| fallvst             | Measures the time difference versus the time of the given signal starting from high y_level to low y_level within the range of x_start and x_stop. |
| fft                 | Measures the Fast-Fourier-Transform (FFT) of a given signal. The signal is evenly Piece-Wise-Constant sampled from x_start to x_stop for n points. |
| flip                | Reverses the signal along the y-axis.                                                                                                              |
| fourEval            | Evaluates the Fourier series represented by the buffer expression.                                                                                 |
| func                | Plots the waveform of signal1 versus signal2 for the two specified signals.                                                                        |
| fvst                | Calculates the frequency versus time for the given signal.                                                                                         |
| gdelay              | Measures the group delay waveform of a given signal.                                                                                               |
| histo               | Generates a histogram waveform for the input signal.                                                                                               |
| hold_times          | This is used to plot a waveform that contains all of the hold time data points.                                                                    |
| hold_times2         | Plots a waveform containing all of the hold time data points.                                                                                      |
| ift                 | Calculates the Inverse Fourier transform (IFT) time domain waveform of the input frequency domain signal.                                          |
| inl                 | Computes the integral non-linearity of a transient simple or parametric waveform.                                                                  |
| integral            | Measures the running integral waveform of the input signal.                                                                                        |
| ipnhVRICurves       | N dB intercept point VRI Curves.                                                                                                                   |
| join                | Generates a joined waveform from signal1 and signal2, which depends on the starting x-axis value of the two signals.                               |

| loadpull            | Generates load pull contour of waveform PSS analysis.                                                                                              |

## a2d

Converts the input signal from analog to digital.

```
Syntax a2d(<signal>,<low_bounds>,<high_bounds>,[<num_of_bits>], [<time_step>],[<x_start>],[<x_stop>], [<single_threshold>],[<delay_to_x>]) Returns A logic signal. Arguments <signal> The analog signal to input. <low_bounds> The low threshold of y. <high_bounds> The high threshold of y. [<num_of_bits>] (Optional) Number of bits to be set. [<time_step>] (Optional) The value of each time_step. [<x_start>] (Optional) The starting point of x. [<x_stop>] (Optional) The ending point of x. [<single_threshold>] (Optional) Specifies the center threshold of y. This argument conflicts with
```

low\_bounds and high\_bounds.

```
[<delay_to_x>] (Optional) Specifies time transferred to x.
```

## Errors

Possible error messages include:

- Signal not found
- Y value out of range
- Bit number can't be greater than 32
- X value out of range

## Examples

```
a2d('0|v(out)',2,4); a2d('0|v(out)',2,4,5,2n,0,10n)
```

## bestfit

Measures the best fit line for a waveform.

## Syntax

```
bestfit(<signal>, [<type>], [<power>])
```

## Returns

A waveform to fit the signal.

## Arguments

```
<signal>
```

The signal or value to be calculated.

```
<type>
```

The method applied to calculate the fitted line. It can be 'Polynominal fitting'(default), 'Exponential fitting', 'Logarithmical fitting', or 'Ratio polynom fitting'.

```
<power>
```

Power value for 'Exponential fitting'. Default value is 1.

## clip

Generates a new waveform whose x range is limited to the given x\_start and x\_stop values. The y range is limited to the given y\_min and y\_max values.

## Syntax

```
clip(<signal>,[<x_start>],[<x_stop>],[<y_min>],[<y_max>],[<percent>]) Returns A waveform. Arguments <signal> The signal to be clipped. [<x_start>] (Optional) The point of x where the clip starts. [<x_stop>] (Optional) The value of x where the clip stops. [<y_min>] (Optional) The low threshold of y.
```

```
[<y_max>] (Optional) The high threshold of y.
```

```
[<percent>]
```

(Optional) The value can be 0 or 1 . If the value is specified as 1 , the y\_threshold is considered as a percentage value. If the value is specified as 0 , the y\_threshold is not considered a percentage value.

## Errors

Possible error messages include:

- Signal not found
- X value out of range
- Y value out of range

## Examples

```
clip('0|v(out)'); clip('0|v(out)',2n,4n,1,3,1)
```

## create\_eye

Creates an eye object which can be plotted as an eye diagram.

## Syntax

```
create_eye(<signal>,[<trigger_signal>],[eye_width], [<user_width/data_rate>],[<trigger_period>], [<start_i>],[<stop_i>],[<start_t>],[<stop_t>],[<phase>])
```

## Returns

An eye object, which is a waveform object that contains eye parameter information.

## Arguments

```
<signal> A transient periodic signal. [<trigger_signal>] The external trigger signal. [eye_width] The eye width type: auto , user , or data_rate . If auto is selected, the eye diagram width is calculated, which is the value to be used for folding the signal. The default is auto . [<user_width/data rate>] The width of the eye diagram, which is a scalar value used to folding the signal. If user is selected as the [eye width] , then the value input in this field is the eye width. If data_rate is selected as the [eye width] , then the value input in this field is the data rate value. [<trigger_period>] The trigger period. [<start_i>] (Optional) The starting edge, which is an index-based filter. [<stop_i>] (Optional) The last edge, which is an index-based filter. [<start_t>] (Optional) The starting time, which is a time-based filter.
```

<!-- image -->

```
Chapter 7: Supported Functions Waveform Functions [<stop_t>] (Optional) The ending time, which is a time-based filter. [<phase>] (Optional) The eye shift. Setting as auto centers the eye opening. .
```

## Errors

Possible error messages are:

- Signal not found
- User width must be specified if not auto width
- Stop\_i must be greater than start\_i
- Stop\_t must be greater than start\_t
- Invalid user input shift value

## dBCPVRICurves

## Description

Creates a signal associated with an nth compression point measurement.

This function extracts the specified harmonic from the input signals, calculates a power waveform through the spectralPower function for given voltage signal and current signal or resistance.

This function then uses the power waveform to extrapolate a constant slope line.

The result signal is a multiple traces signal containing power waveform and the extrapolation line.

## Syntax

```
dBCPVRICurves(<voltage_signal>,<harmonic_index>,[<current_signal>], [<resistance>],[<gainDecrease>],[<extrapolationPoint>],[<sweepUnits>], [<format>])
```

## Returns

A multiple traces signal.

The first trace is the power or gain curve. The second trace is the extrapolation line.

## Arguments

```
<voltage_signal> The input voltage signal, which must be a multiple traces spectrum waveform. <harmonic_index> Harmonic index. <current_signal> (Optional) The input current signal, which must be a multiple traces spectrum
```

waveform.

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

```
<resistance> (Optional) Resistance into the output port. Default value is 50 Ohm. <gainDecrease> (Optional) The delta between power waveform and ideal gain line. <extrapolationPoint> (Optional) The X value (in dBm) indicating the power waveform point that constant slope extrapolation line crosses. Default is the first point of the power waveform. <sweepUnits> (Optional) Can be dBm , W , or none . Default is dBm . <format> (Optional) Can be power or gain . Default is power .
```

```
The signal to be measured. <reference_signal> The reference signal. <signal_y_level> Threshold level for trigger signal. <reference_signal y_level> Threshold level for reference signal.
```

<!-- image -->

```
[<percent>] (Optional) The value can be 1 or 0 . When specified as 1 , the y_threshold is a percentage value; when specified as 0 , the threshold is not a percentage value. [<trigger_type>] (Optional) The trigger_type of measured signal, which can be fall , rise , or either . The default value is either . [<reference_trigger_type>] (Optional) The trigger_type of reference signal, which can be fall, rise, same, opposite, and either. Default is either. [<x1_start>] The starting value of x for trigger signal. [<x1_stop>] (Optional) The stopping value of x for trigger signal. [<x2_start>] (Optional) The starting value of x for reference signal. [<x2_stop>] (Optional) The stopping value of x for reference signal. [<premise>] Specifies the delay value as positive , negative , or either . Errors Possible error messages include: · Signal not found · Y value out of range Examples delayvst('0|v(out)','0|v(out)',4,3); delayvst('0|v(out)','0|v(out)',4,3,0,2,4,10n,'fall', reftrig='same',x1start=1n,x1stop=4n,x2start=2n,x2stop=5n)

## dft

Measures the Discrete-Fourier-Transform (DFT) of a given signal. The signal is evenly Piece-Wise-Constant sampled from x\_start to x\_stop for n points.

## Syntax

```
dft(<signal>,<x_start>,<x_stop>,<num_of_points>, [<windowing_type>],[<window_alpha>], [<normalization>],[<user_defined_value>], [<suppress_DC>], [<dual_sideband>], [<coherent_gain>],[<coherent_gain_factor>], [<ADC_span>],[<window_sampling>]) Returns A waveform. Arguments <signal> The signal to be measured. <x_start> The starting point of x. <x_stop> The ending point of x. <num_of_points> The number of points needing to be measured. [<windowing_type>] (Optional) Specifies the windowing function. The default is a rectangle. [<windowing_alpha>] (Optional) Windowing alpha is only applicable for Kaiser, Kaiser-bessel, and Gaussian window types. Accepts values from 1.0 to 20.0. The default is 3.0.
```

<!-- image -->

```
[<normalization>]
```

(Optional) There are three options for this argument:

- none - FFT results is not normalized.
- normalized - FFT results is normalized against the maximum magnitude value of the waveform.
- user-defined - FFT results is normalized against a user-defined magnitude value.

```
[<user_defined_value>]
```

(Optional) This argument is only applicable if [&lt;normalization&gt;] is set to userdefined.

```
[<suppress_dc>]
```

(Optional) If set to true, the DC component is excluded from the target waveforms in the FFT/DFT operation. This is to minimize the error introduced by those signals with large DC component and very small AC magnitudes.

```
[<dual_sideband>]
```

(Optional) If this argument is set to false, the resultant waveform is only on one side of the Y-axis starting from 0 to N-1. When set to true, the resultant waveform is symmetric to the Y-axis from -N/2 to N/2.

```
[<coherent_gain>]
```

(Optional) This argument specifies coherent gain factor type (none, default, magnitude, db20, db10). The coherent gain factor value is used to scale the power spectral density results.

- none: no scaling the results
- default: scaling the results by 1, if the window type is a rectangle. Else, scaling the results to the signal's amplitude.
- magnitude: scaling with coherent\_gain\_factor
- dB20: scaling with pow(10,coherent\_gain\_fator/20)
- dB10: scaling with pow(10,coherent\_gain\_factor/10)

```
[<coherent_gain_factor>]
```

(Optional) Specifies the scaling factor. A non-zero value that scales the power spectral density by 1/(Coherent Gain). Valid values are 0 &lt; 1. Default is 0. You can use 1 if you do not want this scaling factor to be used.

<!-- image -->

```
[<ADC_span>]
```

(Optional) Specifies the peak saturation level of the FFT waveform. When specified the magnitude of the input waveform is divided by ADC span value before computing FFT. This is full-scale span, ignoring any DC offsets. Valid values are any floating point number. Default value is 1.0.

```
[<window_sampling>]
```

(Optional) Determines whether the window samples are computed in a periodic or a symmetric manner. For example, when set to periodic, the window will be extended by 1 sample. The default is symmetric.

## Errors

Possible error messages include:

- Signal not found
- Y value out of range
- Number of sample points is non-positive
- X value out of range

## Examples

```
dft('0|v(out)',2n,4n,2); dft('0|v(out)',2n,4n,2,'rectangle');
```

## dnl

## Description

Computes the differential non-linearity of a transient waveform. DNL is calculated as:

where 0 &lt; D &lt; 2 N -2.

## Syntax

```
dnl(<signal>,<sampling_signal|list|step>,[<cross_type>], [<mode>],[<threshold>],[<delay>],[<method>],[<unit>], [<no_of_samples>])
```

## Returns

An analog signal.

## Arguments

&lt;signal&gt;

The signal to be measured.

&lt;sampling\_signal|list|step&gt;

This argument specifies three ways to sampling the waveform:

- sampling\_signal: the measured the signal is sampled according to the input sampling signal. The sample points is obtained at which the waveform crosses the threshold (specified with [&lt;mode&gt;] and [&lt;threshold&gt;] options) at either rising or falling edge (specified with [&lt;cross\_type&gt;] option). The sampling can start with a delay (specified with [&lt;delay&gt;] option).
- list: list of x values at which the sample points are obtained for the measured signal.
- step: the interval value specified for sampling the measured signal.

<!-- formula-not-decoded -->

(Optional) Specifies the edge types at which the sampling signal intersect with the threshold. There are two options: rising or falling.

<!-- image -->

```
[<mode>]
```

(Optional) Specifies the mode used to calculate the threshold value. There are two options:

- user: Specify the threshold value with [&lt;threshold&gt;] option.
- auto: the threshold is calculated automatically by (integral\_of\_waveform / x\_range).

```
[<threshold>]
```

(Optional) Specifies the threshold value used to sample the data. Only specified if mode is user .

```
[<delay>]
```

(Optional) Specifies time after which the sampling begins.

```
[<method>]
```

(Optional) Specifies whether the end-to-end (end) or straight line (fit) method is used.

```
[<unit>]
```

(Optional) Specifies whether the output waveform is to be output as an absolute value (abs) or multiples of least significant bit (lsb).

```
[<no_of_samples>]
```

(Optional) Specifies the samples used for calculating the non-linearity. If not specified, the samples are taken against the entire data window.

<!-- image -->

## Examples

The following example shows how the function works on the input waveform 'v(node\_cos1)':

<!-- image -->

The example inputs of the arguments show as follows:

- signal: v(node\_cos1)
- step: 10m
- npts: 1024

The function expression shows as follows:

```
dnl('v(node_cos1)',10m,'rising',npts=1024)
```

## join

Generates a joined waveform from signal1 and signal2 , which depends on the starting x-axis value of the two signals. The waveform that has the greater starting x value is always appended to the one with the smaller x starting value. If signal1 and signal2 overlap, the overlapped portion of the latter waveform is removed before joining. For the reversed sweep data whose x starting value &gt;x stopping value from the two signals, signal1 and signal2 is reordered into a forward sweep in the joined waveform.

join(<signal1>,<signal2>) Returns A waveform. Arguments <signal1>
```

The first input signal. <signal2> The second input signal.
```

- Signal not found

join('0|v(out)','0|v(out)')
```

## jvst\_freq

## Description

Calculates the jitter versus time given the frequency of an ideal clock for the following jitter types:

- N-Cycle and N-Period Jitter

N-Cycle jitter extends cycle-to-cycle jitter. Instead of measuring the difference between adjacent periods, a multiple grouping of N periods is measured. Where N = 3, the width of three periods is measured. N can be any value from 2 to n where only the available sample population limits n. Once again, after taking a significant sample of periods and measuring the differences in the multiple groupings, the standard deviation and peak values can be resolved. This statistical information is the N-Cycle 'jitter.' There are two permutations of the N-Cycle jitter. The first reports statistics from the difference between adjacent groupings (best called N-Cycle jitter). The second reports statistics from the variation of the multiple periods (best called N-Period jitter).

- Pulse Width Jitter

Measures the pulse differences between the reference signal and the target signal at the reference edge.

- Period Jitter

Measures the period differences between the reference signal and the target signal at the reference edge.

- Cycle-to-cycle Jitter

The application of simple arithmetic to the period measurements just taken. If the timing information for the two adjacent periods is known, the difference between them is the cycle-to-cycle change: period one minus period two. Again, after taking a significant sample of periods, and measuring the difference between them, the standard deviation and peak values can be resolved. This statistical information is the cycle-to-cycle 'jitter'.

<!-- image -->

## Syntax

```
jvst_freq(<signal>,<jitter_type>,<clock_freq>,<y_at_rise>, <y_at_fall>,<clock_edge>,[<signal_edge>], [<number_of_periods>],[<search_forward>], [<search_range>],[<value_sign>],[<percent>]) Returns A waveform. Arguments <signal> The signal to be measured. <jitter_type> The jitter type can be trigger , width , period , cycle , nperiod , or ncycle . <clock_freq> Frequency for an ideal reference clock. <y_at_rise> The input signal threshold level at the rising edge. <y_at_fall> The input signal threshold level at the falling edge. <clock_edge> The reference signal_edge type. The default type is rise , however the type can also be same , fall , or both . [<signal_edge>] The type of input signal_edge . The default type is rise , however the type can also be same , fall , or both . [<number_of_periods>] (Optional) Only one nperiod and ncycle is specified for the jitter_type . The default is 1 for n period. [<search_forward>] (Optional) Always search forward for the target edge. Values can be 0 or 1 . The default value is 0 . [<search_range>] (Optional) The maximum target edge search range.
```

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

```
Waveform Functions [<value_sign>] (Optional) The forward or backward positive value sign. Values can be 0 or 1 . The default value is 0 , which represents the forward positive value_sign . [<percent>] (Optional) The value can be 1 or 0 . When the value is 1 , the y_threshold is a percentage value. If the value is 0 , the y_threshold is not percentage value. Errors Possible error messages include: · Signal not found · Incorrect signal type · Invalid input value · Frequency value can't be 0 · Unknown target edge type, should be same, rise, fall, or cross Examples jvst_freq('0|v(out)','width',2.5E8,3,2,'rise') jvst_freq('0|v(out)','width',2.5E8,3,2,'rise','same',nperiod=1,forward=0, range=10n,sign=0,percent=1) jvst_ideal Calculates the jitter versus time with an ideal clock. Syntax jvst_ideal(<signal>,<jitter_type>,<clock_delay>, <clock_period>,<clock_width>,<y_at_rise>,<y_at_fall>, <clock_edge>[,<signal_edge>][,<num_of_periods>][ <search_forward>][,<search_range>][,<value_sign>][,<percent>]) Returns A waveform. Arguments <signal> The signal to be measured. <jitter_type> The jitter type can be trigger , width , period , cycle , nperiod , or ncycle .
```

<!-- image -->

<clock_delay> Delays the time value for an ideal reference clock with a period value. <clock_period> Period value for reference ideal clock. <clock_width> Width value for an ideal reference clock. Note that the value of clock_width should always be smaller than the value of clock_period . <y_at_rise> The input signal threshold level at the rising edge. <y_at_fall> The input signal threshold level at the falling edge. <clock_edge> The reference signal_edge type. The default type is rise , however the type can also be same , fall , or both . [<signal_edge>] The type of input signal_edge . The default type is rise , however the type can also be same , fall , or both . [<number_of_periods>] (Optional) Only one nperiod and ncycle is specified for the jitter_type . The default is 1 for n period. [<search_forward>] (Optional) Always search forward for the target edge. Values can be 0 or 1 . The default value is 0 . [<search_range>] (Optional) Maximum target edge search range. [<value_sign>] (Optional) Forward or backward positive value sign. The value can be 0 or 1 . The default value is 0 , which represents the forward positive value_sign . [<percent>] (Optional) The value can be 1 or 0 . When the value is 1 , the y_threshold is a percentage value. If the value is 0 , the y_threshold is not percentage value.

## jvst\_llse

## Description

Calculates the jitter versus time with an estimated frequency of the ideal clock using LLSE (Linear Least Squares Estimator).

LLSE creates an X-Y plot, where X is edge number and Y is time of edge occurrence. For the ideal clock, the result is a linear line whose slope equals the period time. For the real clock, the result is a point scattered plot.

To find the closest frequency around which these points are scattered, use LLSE estimator to get the y=aX+b formula of this line. This is useful for the PLL jitter calculation, because sometimes the target frequency of the PLL is unknown, and the jitter can be calculated around the optimal frequency.

## Syntax

```
jvst_llse(<signal>,<jitter_type>,<y_at_rise>, <y_at_fall>, <clock_edge>,[<signal_edge>], [<number_of_periods>],[<search_forward>], [<search_range>],[<value_sign>],[<percent>])
```

## Returns

A waveform.

<!-- image -->

## Arguments

```
<signal> The signal to be measured. <jitter_type> The jitter type can be trigger , width , period , cycle , nperiod , or ncycle . <y_at_rise> The input signal threshold level at the rising edge. <y_at_fall> The input signal threshold level at the falling edge. <clock_edge> The reference signal_edge type. The default type is rise , however the type can also be same , fall , or both . [<signal_edge>] (Optional) The type of input signal_edge . The default type is rise , however the type can also be same , fall , or both . [<number_of_periods>] (Optional) Only one nperiod and ncycle is specified for the jitter_type . The default is 1 for n period. [<search_forward>] (Optional) Always search forward for the target edge. Values can be 0 or 1 . The default value is 0 . [<search_range>] (Optional) Maximum target edge search range. [<value_sign>] (Optional) Forward or backward positive value sign. The value can be 0 or 1 . The default value is 0 , which represents the forward positive value_sign . [<percent>] (Optional) The value can be 1 or 0 . When the value is 1 , the y_threshold is a percentage value. If the value is 0 , the y_threshold is not percentage value.
```

<!-- image -->

## Errors

Possible error messages include:

- Signal not found
- Incorrect signal type
- Invalid input value
- No valid frequency found by Linear Square Estimator
- Unknown jitter type, should be trigger, width, period, cycle, nperiod or ncycle
- Unknown ref edge type, should be rise, fall, or both

## Examples

```
jvst_llse('0|v(out)','width',3,2,'rise','same',nperiod=1, forward=0,range=8n,sign=0 percent=1)
```

## median

Measures the smoothed waveform of the given signal using median value method. For every data point in the original signal, the median value method sorts the values of the original data point and w points window before and after the original point. The median value of the sorted result is then used to replace the original data value.

## Syntax

median(&lt;signal&gt;,&lt;points\_window&gt;)

## Returns

A waveform.

## Arguments

&lt;signal&gt;

The input signal.

&lt;points\_window&gt;

The number of points in the window.

## Errors

Possible error messages include:

- Signal not found
- Invalid input value

## Examples

## optical\_fft

Converts time-domain optical signal waveforms into their equivalent complex optical spectra. The FFT of the optical signal is calculated over the full range of negative and positive frequencies.

## Syntax

```
fft(<optical signal>,<x_start>,<x_stop>,<num_of_points>, [<windowing_type>],[<window_alpha>], [<normalization>],[<user_defined_value>], [<suppress_DC>],[<coherent_gain>], [<coherent_gain_factor>],[<ADC_span>], [<window_sampling>],[<output xAxisType>]) Returns A waveform Arguments <signal> The optical signal to be measured. <x_start> The starting point of x. <x_stop> The ending point of x. <num_of_points> The number of points needing to be measured. Must be a power of 2. [<windowing_type>] (Optional) Specifies the windowing function. The default is a rectangle. [<window_alpha>] (Optional) Window alpha is only applicable for Kaiser, Kaiser-bessel, and Gaussian window types. Accepts values from 1.0 to 20.0. The default is 3.0.
```

<!-- image -->

```
[<normalization>]
```

(Optional) There are three options for this argument:

- none - optical\_fft results are not normalized.
- normalized - optical\_fft results are normalized against the maximum magnitude value of the waveform.
- user-defined - optical\_fft results are normalized against a user-defined magnitude value.

```
[<user_defined_value>]
```

(Optional) This argument is only applicable if normalization is set to userdefined.

```
[<suppress_dc>]
```

(Optional) If set to true, the DC component is excluded from the target waveforms in the FFT/DFT operation. This is to minimize the error introduced by those signals with large DC component and very small AC magnitudes.

```
[<coherent_gain>]
```

(Optional) This argument specifies coherent gain factor type (none, default, magnitude, db20, db10). The coherent gain factor value is used to scale the power spectral density results.

- none: no scaling the results
- default: scaling the results by 1 if the window type is a rectangle. Else, scaling the results to the signal's amplitude.
- magnitude: scaling with coherent\_gain\_factor
- dB20: scaling with pow (10, coherent\_gain\_factor/20)
- dB10: scaling with pow (10, coherent\_gain\_factor/10)

```
[<coherent_gain_factor>]
```

(Optional) Specifies the scaling factor. A non-zero value that scales the power spectral density by 1/(Coherent Gain). Valid values are 0 &lt; 1. Default is 0. You can use 1 if you do not want this scaling factor to be used.

```
[<ADC_span>]
```

(Optional) Specifies the peak saturation level of the FFT waveform. When specified the magnitude of the input waveform is divided by ADC span value before computing FFT. This is full-scale span, ignoring any DC offsets. Valid values are any floating point number. Default is 1.0.

<!-- image -->

```
[<window_sampling>]
```

(Optional) Determines whether the window samples are computed in a periodic or a symmetric manner. For example, when set to periodic, the window will be extended by 1 sample. Default is symmetric.

```
[<output xAxis Type>]
```

(Optional) Determines the X Axis type of the result spectra, two options are available:

- opticalWavelength: Optical Wavelength, calculated by C/F, where C is the speed of light, F is the optical frequency.
- opticalFrequency: Optical Frequency, calculated by F=f+C/wavelength, where f is the frequency value.

## Errors

Possible error messages include:

- Signal not found
- Y value out of range
- Number of sample points is non-positive
- Number of sample points is not power of 2
- X value out of range

## psd

## Description

Power spectral density. Describes how the power of a signal or time series is distributed with frequency. This function estimates Power Spectral Density using the overlapped segmented averaging of periodograms method. A periodogram is the DFT of one segment of the signal or time series.

## Syntax

```
psd(<signal>,<x_start>,<x_stop>,<num_of_points>, [<windowing_type>],[<window_alpha>], [<window_size>],[<detrend_mode>], [<coherent_gain>],[<coherent_gain_factor>])
```

## Returns

An analog signal.

<!-- image -->

## Arguments

```
<signal> The signal to be calculated. <x_start> Starting time for the spectral analysis interval. <x_stop> Ending time for the spectral analysis interval. <num_of_points> Number of time domain points to be used. Default value is 512. [<windowing_type>] (Optional) Specifies window to be used. [<windowing_alpha>] This argument is only applicable for Kaiser, Kaiser-bessel, and Gaussian window types. Accepts values from 0 to 15. The value 0 implies no smoothing and is equivalent to a rectangular window. The default value is 1. [<window_size>] (Optional) Number of frequency domain points to use in the Fourier analysis. [<detrend_mode>] (Optional) Specifies the trend mode (linear, mean, none).
```

- linear: compute a least squares regression line for each segment and subtract that line from the data points of the segment
- mean: subtract the average value from the data points of the segment
- none (default): no trend removal

```
[<coherent_gain>]
```

(Optional) This argument specifies coherent gain factor type (none, default, magnitude, db20, db10). The coherent gain factor value is used to scale the power spectral density results.

- none: no scaling the results
- default: scaling the results by 1 if the window type is a rectangle. Else, scaling the results to the signal's amplitude.
- magnitude: scaling with coherent\_gain\_factor

<!-- image -->

```
· dB20: scaling with pow(10,coherent_gain_fator/20) · dB10: scaling with pow(10,coherent_gain_factor/10) [<coherent_gain_factor>]
```

(Optional) Specifies the scaling factor. A non-zero value that scales the power spectral density by 1/(Coherent Gain). Valid values are 0 &lt; 1. Default is 0. You can use 1 if you do not want this scaling factor to be used.

## psdbb

## Description

Power spectral density baseband. Returns an estimate for the power spectral density of a waveform1+j * waveform2.

## Syntax

```
psdbb(<signal1>,<signal2>,<x_start>,<x_stop>, <num_of_points>,[<windowing_type>],[<window_alpha>], [<window_size>],[<detrending_mode>], [<coherent_gain>],[<coherent_gain_factor>]) Returns An analog signal. Arguments <signal1> First signal to be calculated. <signal2> Second signal to be calculated. <x_start> Starting time for the spectral analysis interval. <x_stop> Ending time for the spectral analysis interval. <num_of_points> Number of time domain points to be used. Default value is 512. [<windowing_type>] (Optional) Specifies window to be used.
```

<!-- image -->

```
[<windowing_alpha>]
```

This argument is only applicable for Kaiser, Kaiser-bessel, and Gaussian window types. Accepts values from 0 to 15. The value 0 implies no smoothing and is equivalent to a rectangular window. The default value is 1.

```
[<window_size>]
```

(Optional) Specifies number of frequency domain points to use in the Fourier analysis. A larger window size results in an expectation operation over fewer samples, which leads to larger variations in the power spectral density. A small window size can smear out sharp steps in the power spectral density that might be present. Default value is 256.

```
[<detrending_mode>]
```

(Optional) Specifies the trend mode (linear, mean, none). If there is a deterministic trend to the underlying data, you might want to remove the trend before performing the spectral analysis. For example, consider analyzing phase noise in a VCO model. Without the noise, the phase increases more or less linearly with time, so it is appropriate to set the mode to linear.

To subtract an average value, set the to mean. If the spectrum of raw data is desired, set the mode to none. Default value is none.

```
[<coherent_gain>]
```

(Optional) Specifies the zero frequency gain (or the DC gain) of the window. When performing dft, the applied window type (aside from the rectangular type) changes the signal amplitude. Applying a coherent gain factor is a way to get consistent results regardless of the window type. Valid Values are none, default, magnitude, dB20, or dB10.

```
[<coherent_gain_factor>]
```

(Optional) Specifies the scaling factor. A non-zero value that scales the power spectral density by 1/(Coherent Gain). Valid values are 0 &lt; 1. Default is 0. You can use 1 if you do not want this scaling factor to be used.

If the input value for the clock_signal period is 0 or less than 0 , the clock_period is calculated using the clock_signal . <y_threshold> The threshold value of y for the measured signal. <signal_edge> The type of measured signal_edge . The valid signal_edge can be rise ,
```

```
fall , or both . The default signal_edge is rise .
```

<!-- image -->

```
<clock_edge> The type of reference clock_signal edge. The valid signal_edge can be rise , fall , or both . The default signal_edge is rise . [<x_start>] (Optional) The starting time of measurement. [<x_stop>] (Optional) The ending time of measurement. [<percent>] (Optional) The value can be 1 or 0 . When the value is 1 , the y_threshold is a percentage value. ## setup\_times2

Generates a new waveform that contains all of the setup time data points. setup\_times2 differs from setup\_times in that it gives you the ability to specify a different threshold for the clock signal as well as the measured signal, whereas setup\_times allows selecting the threshold of only the measured signal.

## Syntax

```
setup_times2(<signal>,<clock_signal>,<clock_period>, <data_threshold>,<clock_threshold>,<signal_edge>, <clock_edge>,[<x_start>],[<x_stop>],[<percent>])
```

## Returns

A waveform.

## Arguments

```
<signal> The signal to be measured. <clock_signal> The reference clock signal. <clock_period> The period of the reference clock_signal . If the input value for the clock_signal period is 0 or less than 0 , the clock_period is calculated using the clock_signal . <data_threshold> The threshold value of y for the measured signal. <clock_threshold> The threshold value of y for the clock_signal . <signal_edge> The type of measured signal_edge . The valid signal_edge can be rise , fall , or both . The default signal_edge is rise . <clock_edge> The type of reference clock_signal edge. The valid signal_edge can be rise , fall , or both . The default signal_edge is rise . [<x_start>] (Optional) The starting time of measurement. [<x_stop>] (Optional) The ending time of measurement. [<percent>] (Optional) The value can be 1 or 0 . When the value is 1 , the y_threshold is a percentage value. If the value is 0 , the y_threshold is not a percentage value.
```

## Errors

Possible error messages include:

- Signal not found
- Incorrect signal type

<!-- image -->

- Y value out of range
- X value out of range

## Examples

```
setup_times2('0|v(out)','0|v(out)',4n,2,3,'rise','rise') setup_times2('0|v(out)','0|v(out)',4n,2,3,'rise','rise',2n 6n,1)
```

| ga         | A 2-port available power gain.                                                                                            |
| gac_freq   | The available power gain circles where the gain is fixed and frequency is swept.                                          |
| gac_gain   | The available power gain circles where the frequency is fixed and gain is swept.                                          |

| gmin       | The optimum noise reflection coefficient for nfmin.                                                                       |
| gmsg       | A 2-port max. stable power gain.                                                                                          |
| gp         | A 2-port power gain.                                                                                                      |
| gpc_freq   | The operating power gain circles where the gain is fixed and frequency is swept.                                          |
| gpc_gain   | The operating power gain circles where the frequency is fixed and gain is swept.                                          |
| gt         | A 2-port transducer power gain.                                                                                           |
| gumx       | A 2-port unilateral max. available power gain.                                                                            |
| harmonic   | Returns the signal value for a specific intermodulation product.                                                          |
| hp         | 2-port H-parameter, p1/p2 1-based port index. z0: port characteristic impedance.                                          |
| imProd     | Calculates the intermodulation produce of a given signal and frequency.                                                   |
| kf         | A 2-port stability factor.                                                                                                |
| lsb        | Returns the load stability circles.                                                                                       |
| lq         | Calculates the Inductance value L and Quality factor Q.                                                                   |
| mu1        | U-test for stability circle derivation.                                                                                   |
| mu2        | U-test for stability circle derivation.                                                                                   |
| nc_freq    | Noise circles with fixed frequency.                                                                                       |
| nc_gain    | Noise circles with fixed frequency.                                                                                       |

|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| nf         | The noise figure of the waveform file.                                                                                                                                                       |
| nfmin      | The minimum noise figure.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| noisec     | Calculates the noise circle over input Noise Figure values at specified frequency values.                                                                                                    |
| opgc       | Calculates the Operating Power Gain Circles over S-parameter values and gain values at specified frequency values.                                                                           |
| rn         | Normalized equivalent noise resistance vs. frequency waveform.                                                                                                                               |
| Rn         | Equivalent noise resistance vs. frequency waveform.                                                                                                                                          |

| ssb        | Returns the source stability circles.                                                                                                                                                        |
